rows.ca_value: Amendment No. 9 to the existing 2019 Credit Agreement, entered into as an Incremental Amendment under Section 2.14. It establishes (ii) Refinancing Incremental Revolving Credit Commitments and (iii) a $250,000,000 Incremental Revolving Credit Facility; together these become the Initial Revolving Credit Commitments. The same amendment refinances all existing term loans with Amendment No. 9 Term Loans and adds swingline loans (Section 2.18). The conformed Amended Credit Agreement is Exhibit A.
rows.ca_quote: (ii) "Refinancing Incremental Revolving Credit Commitments" and (iii) an "Incremental Revolving Credit Facility" in an aggregate amount of $250,000,000

rows.explanation: Same substance: an amend, extend and upsize of the existing secured RCF, with a new swingline. The CA does it through refinancing-incremental and incremental commitments rather than a plain amendment. It also puts the TLB refinancing in the same Amendment No. 9, which the TS presented as a parallel transaction. These are differences of mechanics, not economics.

The CA instead fixes S+150 (Level 3) until the Compliance Certificate for the quarter ending June 30, 2026 is delivered. That certificate is due with the quarterly financials within 60 days (Sections 7.01(b) and 7.02(a)), so the fixed period runs to about late August 2026, and drawn pricing is 25 bps higher during it. Strike-through decoding shows the 1.50%/0.50% figures are unamended text; only the reference date changed (2025 Revolving Incremental Amendment to Amendment No. 9). This is a common market mechanic, but it is not in the TS.

rows.ts_location: PDF p.11, Summary of Indicative Terms (Undrawn Fee)
rows.ca_value:
Commitment Fee:
- Fixed at 0.375% until the Compliance Certificate for the first FULL fiscal quarter ending after the Amendment No. 9 Effective Date is delivered (the prior 0.50% and "Closing" are struck). The quarter ending June 30, 2026 began before the May 14, 2026 effective date, so the first full quarter is likely the one ending September 30, 2026, with the certificate due within 60 days (about late November 2026). By contrast, the margin lock in A12 runs only to the first fiscal quarter.
- Thereafter 0.375% if First Lien Net Leverage >2.75x, or 0.25% if <=2.75x (the prior 0.50%/0.375% grid is struck).
Charged on the average daily unused commitments. Swingline loans do not count as usage. Paid quarterly in arrears.
rows.ca_quote: 0.375% per annum if the First Lien Net Leverage Ratio as of the most recent determination date is greater than 2.75 to 1.00 or (y) 0.25% per annum if the First Lien Net Leverage Ratio as of the most recent determination date is less than or equal to 2.75 to 1.00.
rows.ca_location: Exhibit A Section 1.01 "Applicable Rate" clause (d)(i)-(ii), PDF p.45; Section 2.09(a), PDF p.140-141; Section 7.01(b), PDF p.185
rows.explanation: Both fee levels (37.5 / 25 bps) and the 2.75x threshold (<= for the stepdown) match the TS, and strike-through decoding confirms the inserted 0.375%/0.25% text is the operative text. However, the CA adds a condition the TS does not state: the stepdown is locked out until the first full-quarter Compliance Certificate after closing. The TS shows pro forma First Lien Net Leverage of 1.0x (PDF p.10), which is within the 25 bps tier, so under the TS the stepdown would apply from closing. The lockout costs the borrower 12.5 bps on undrawn commitments for roughly the first six months. This is the same initial-period mechanic as A12, so it is treated the same way. It is minor because it is market-standard and limited in time.

TS: the TS is not a formal term sheet. It is a Citigroup "Revolving Lender Presentation" dated April 2026, with a Company Authorization Letter dated April 30, 2026. The economic terms are on PDF p.10 (Executive Summary) and PDF p.11 (Summary of Indicative Terms, headed "Indicative Pricing"). PDF p.12-13 cover sources and uses and the timeline. The rest is disclaimers, Q1'26 financials and contacts. The p.11 pricing grid and the p.12 tables are garbled in the text extraction. The relational symbols in the grid were lost in extraction ("<" survived; the inclusive symbols did not), so the tiers were read as >=3.50x / <3.50x & >=2.50x / <2.50x & >=1.50x / <1.50x. That reading is supported by the tier structure: the upper bounds are strict ("<3.50x", "<2.50x"), so the lower bounds must be inclusive to leave no gap. It also matches the CA. The TS PDF itself (PDF 1.6 with compressed object streams) could not be rendered to confirm the glyphs.

CA: the CA is Amendment No. 9 to Credit Agreement, dated May 14, 2026, between APi Group DE, Inc. (Borrower), APi Group Corporation (Holdings) and Citibank, N.A. (Administrative and Collateral Agent). It is an Incremental Amendment under Section 2.14. It does three things:
- (a) sets up Refinancing Incremental Revolving Credit Commitments plus a $250,000,000 Incremental Revolving Credit Facility, for $1,000,000,000 total revolving commitments;
- (b) refinances all existing term loans with $2,157,391,086.86 of Amendment No. 9 Term Loans;
- (c) attaches the conformed Amended Credit Agreement as Exhibit A (PDF p.31-255).
The original agreement is dated October 1, 2019 and was amended nine times. Schedule I (lender allocations and L/C commitments) is on PDF p.29. The reconciliation is against the agreement as amended.

Limitations and review notes:
- The CA PDF was regenerated with ReportLab and is entirely black text. In the extracted .txt, deleted (strike-through) and inserted (underlined) text run together, for example "0.500.375%" and "$750,000,0001,000,000,000". Amendment Section 2(b) describes insertions as blue double-underlined; the regenerated PDF draws single lines.
- pdftoppm was not available. The reviewer independently decoded the ReportLab content streams (read-only, standard-library Python) and matched each drawn line to text-run positions using the embedded TrueType width tables. A line about 2.6pt above the baseline is a strike; a line about 2pt below is an underline. This independently confirmed the following:
  - PDF p.44: the RCF margin grid is unamended apart from replacing the "<"/">" symbols with words. Clause (b) keeps the initial 1.50%/0.50%, with only the reference date changed to Amendment No. 9.
  - PDF p.45: commitment fee 0.375% initially; then 0.375% above 2.75x and 0.25% at or below 2.75x. The old 0.50%/0.375% text is struck.
  - PDF p.78: commitments of $1,000,000,000, with $750,000,000 struck.
  - PDF p.79: the 2021 Incremental Term Loan springing-maturity proviso is struck.
  - PDF p.204-205: the Section 8.02(p) ratios moved from 3.25/3.50/3.75x to 3.75/4.00/4.25x.
  - PDF p.29: Schedule I row alignment of lenders to amounts.
  - No substantive strikes on the other pages relied on (p.42-43, 48, 50, 61, 74, 80, 107, 122-123, 132-141, 144-146, 154, 158).
- Caveats on the decoding: cross-references and some emphasis words (for example "provided") are also underlined in the regenerated PDF, so an underline alone does not prove insertion. Some genuinely new text (for example the swingline definitions on PDF p.109-110) carries no underline.
- Upfront fees are not in the CA. Exhibit A Section 2.09(b) refers to fees "separately agreed upon in writing". Amendment No. 9 Section 4(c)(ii) makes payment of fees separately agreed with the Lead Arrangers a closing condition. No fee letter was provided.
- The initial-period mechanics differ between margin and commitment fee. The margin is fixed at Level 3 until the Compliance Certificate for the first fiscal quarter after May 14, 2026 (Q2 2026). The commitment fee is fixed at 0.375% until the certificate for the first full fiscal quarter (likely Q3 2026). Certificates are due within 60 days of quarter end (Sections 7.01(b) and 7.02(a)).
- Schedules other than Schedule I (for example Schedule 2.01 and 11.02) were not reviewed.
- Covenant, guarantor, security and negative-covenant terms in the TS (PDF p.11) are outside attribute group A and were not reconciled here. The TS's $500mm senior unsecured debt is a separate issuance outside the CA (noted in X01).

TS: \"Exhibit B - Summary of Terms and Conditions\" to a Commitment Letter for a $2,000,000,000 364-Day Revolving Credit Facility for Accenture Capital Inc., Accenture Global Capital DAC and Accenture Finance Limited, guaranteed by Accenture plc. It is marked \"[CS&M Draft--03/26/2026]\" and has Addendum I (Fees and Interest Rates) on PDF pages 9-11. It is a formal term sheet. The closing date is left blank (\"April [], 2026\"). The TS says the CA will be based on the Existing Credit Agreement dated May 14, 2024 (JPMorgan as agent), subject to \"Documentation Principles\". The TS left-hand headings on PDF pages 2-6 are bunched together in the -layout text, but the body text order follows them.

CA: a new standalone \"364-Day Credit Agreement\" dated as of April 22, 2026, marked EXECUTION VERSION, with Bank of America, N.A. as Administrative Agent (145 PDF pages; CA internal page 1 = PDF page 9). It is not an amendment. s.10.22 (PDF page 129) waives the notice for terminating the Existing Credit Agreement. The companion Five-Year Credit Agreement is defined (PDF page 32) as a new agreement dated as of the Closing Date with Bank of America as agent.

Limitations:
(1) Schedule 2.01 (commitments by lender) is not in the text extraction (PDF page 145 has no text), so the total commitment comes from the \"Aggregate Commitments\" definition.
(2) The TS pricing grid on PDF page 10 is jumbled in the -layout text file, and the PDF could not be rendered as an image (pdftoppm is not installed). Re-extracting that page with Xpdf 'pdftotext -simple2' to stdout gives clean rows that confirm the tiers and match the CA grid (PDF page 13) exactly. The TS grid quote is still taken from the jumbled text file because quotes must match that file.
(3) The CA text is not in layout format, and the \"1/2\" character in the Base Rate definition is garbled.
(4) Neither document states the size of the Five-Year Facility, so whether the increase-option caps are equivalent cannot be fully checked. Equivalence would need a $5.325bn Five-Year Facility.

rows.attribute: Required lenders, voting and sacred rights
rows.ts_value: Required Lenders: more than 50% of credit exposures and unused commitments. Consent of all affected Lenders is needed for: (i) commitment increases; (ii) reductions of principal, interest or fees; (iii) extensions of maturity or payment dates, except the Term-Out; (iv) release of the Guarantor; (v) changes to pro rata sharing or the waterfall, the Required Lenders definition and voting provisions, or the alternative currency provisions.

rows.ca_value: Required Lenders: more than 50% of Revolving Exposures and unused Commitments, excluding Defaulting Lenders. Section 10.01(a) requires: (i) the affected Lender's consent to extend or increase its Commitment; (ii) each directly affected Lender to postpone payments, except the 2.04(b) term-out; (iii) each directly affected Lender to reduce principal, rate or fees, though Required Lenders alone can amend the Default Rate; (iv) every Lender for a change to Section 2.11 (sharing) or Section 8.03 (waterfall), but only one 'that would alter the pro rata sharing of payments'; (v) each affected Lender for Section 1.05 or the Alternative Currency definition; (vi) every Lender for voting provisions; (vii) every Lender to release Accenture plc. The AA must consent to changes affecting its rights, and Borrowing Affiliates are protected. Section 10.01(b) limits Defaulting Lender votes, lets the AA and Borrowing Agent correct errors, and allows an amend-and-restate that removes a fully paid-out Lender without its consent.
rows.ca_quote: Lenders having Revolving Exposures and unused Commitments representing in the aggregate more than 50% of the sum of the Revolving Exposures and unused Commitments of all Lenders at such time

One narrowing: the TS protects any modification to the pro rata sharing or waterfall provisions, but the CA protects changes to 2.11/8.03 only where they alter pro rata sharing. Required Lenders could therefore reorder the 8.03 waterfall. On the other hand, the CA needs every Lender, not just affected Lenders, for items (iv), (vi) and (vii). The CA also adds standard mechanics: Defaulting Lender exclusion, a Required-Lender-only Default Rate waiver, AA error correction, and Borrowing Affiliate protections.

result.document_notes: TS: "Exhibit B - Summary of Terms and Conditions" attached to a Commitment Letter, marked "[CS&M Draft--03/26/2026]", for a $2,000,000,000 364-Day Revolving Credit Facility for Accenture Capital Inc., Accenture Global Capital DAC and Accenture Finance Limited, guaranteed by Accenture plc. It has 11 PDF pages, including Addendum I on fees and interest rates (pp.9-11). Many TS terms say "substantially similar to the Existing Credit Agreement" (Credit Agreement dated May 14, 2024, JPMorgan as agent), and that agreement was not provided, so those items can only be checked against what the TS states. In the TS text, the left-column headings are often shifted away from their paragraphs, so headings were assigned by section order. One TS quote (B04) contains the heading "JOINT BOOKRUNNERS:" in the middle because of that layout. CA: a new agreement, not an amendment. It is the executed "EXECUTION VERSION" 364-Day Credit Agreement dated as of April 22, 2026, with Bank of America, N.A. as Administrative Agent. The CA text is a reflowed (non-layout) extraction of 145 PDF pages; body page n = PDF page n+8. Signature pages are PDF pp.130-144: Loan Parties on p.130, the AA on p.131, and 13 Lenders on pp.132-144. Schedule 2.01 (Commitments) and the Exhibits are not in the text (p.145 is blank), so individual lender commitments could not be checked. All original and replacement quotes were machine-checked against both text files with whitespace collapsed, and all were found. Left to Group A: the CA aggregate commitments of US$2,175,000,000 (TS: $2,000,000,000), the US$9,500,000,000 combined accordion, the term-out, and the TS p.8 rate-selection and benchmark-replacement provisions. Main Group B finding (confirmed): the CA cross-default and judgment-default thresholds are US$500,000,000, against $250,000,000 in the TS, a material, borrower-favourable difference. Review changes: X04 is now 'differs' because the CA has no SEC-filings delivery covenant, though TS covenant (i) lists one. B08 is now match_minor_drafting because CA 7.02(b) tests sales of all or substantially all assets only for the Accenture Group as a whole, not per Loan Party, and the negative pledge covers only borrowed-money liens. X08 is now match_minor_drafting because the willful-misconduct exception is limited to direct damages. B14's description of the 2.11/8.03 sacred right is corrected (it covers only changes that alter pro rata sharing). B12's explanation is expanded. Two location references are fixed (B16, X05). Rows X18 (multicurrency option), X19 (day count) and X20 (interest payment dates) were added: all match, and they may overlap with the Group A benchmark, sublimit and interest-period review.

rows.ts_value: Parent may request one-year extensions on each anniversary of the Revolving Effective Date (no stated limit on the number). Request window: no earlier than 60 and no later than 30 days before the anniversary. Lenders respond 20 days before; Agent notifies the Parent 15 days before. The extension is effective only if more than 50% of the Facility Amount is extended or committed. Declining Lenders keep their existing date and may be replaced by third parties reasonably acceptable to the Agent. No term-out option.
rows.ts_quote: The Parent may request that the commitments of each Revolving Lender be extended for additional one year periods by providing notice of such request to the Administrative Agent no earlier than 60 days
rows.ts_location: PDF p.3-4, Extension of Revolving Commitments
rows.ca_value: Borrower Representative (Aon NA) may request a one-year extension 60 to 30 days before any anniversary of the Effective Date. Lender election by a Notice Date 20 days before; Agent notice 15 days before. Effective only if more than 50% of the Aggregate Commitment is extended or assumed. Non-Extending Lenders keep their prior date and may be replaced by Eligible Assignees. Lenders that do not respond are deemed Non-Extending. Subject to the s.4.5 conditions. No term-out option.
rows.ca_quote: request that each Lender extend such Lender's Facility Termination Date for an additional one year from the Facility Termination Date then in effect with respect to such Lender.
rows.explanation: All timing windows (60/30/20/15 days), the more-than-50% threshold, the one-year increment and the replacement of declining lenders are the same. The CA has the Borrower Representative (Aon NA) make the request instead of the Parent, and it treats lenders that do not respond as Non-Extending. Both are mechanical differences.

rows.ts_value: Parent may increase the Facility Amount after the Revolving Effective Date, no more than once a year, in minimum increments of $10,000,000, by up to $1,800,000,000 (total $4.8bn). Conditions: representations true and no Default or Event of Default. The increase may be offered to existing lenders (allocations set by the Parent and the Agent) or to third parties, each committing at least $5,000,000. The TS conditions for Commitment Increases are "Limited to" representations and no default.
rows.ts_quote: The Parent will have the right after the Revolving Effective Date, no more than once a year, to increase the Facility Amount, in minimum increments of $10,000,000, up to a maximum amount of $1,800,000,000
rows.ts_location: PDF p.3, Commitment Increase; PDF p.9, Conditions Precedent to Advances, Commitment Increases and Commitment Extensions
rows.ca_value: Borrower Representative may request increases no more than once per calendar year, in $10,000,000 or integral multiples of it. Total Commitments are capped at $4,800,000,000 at any time. The increase must take effect at least 30 days before the latest scheduled Facility Termination Date. Eligible Assignees must commit at least $5,000,000. Where the increase is oversubscribed, allocation is agreed by the Borrower Representative in consultation with the Agent. Conditions in s.4.4: no Default or Unmatured Default, and representations true. Under s.2.19(a)(ii) the Article IV conditions must be met on both the request date and the Increase Date. On the Increase Date the Agent must also receive certified board resolutions of each Loan Party and an opinion of counsel (which may be in-house counsel) under s.2.19(c)(i).
rows.ca_quote: in no event shall the aggregate amount of the Commitments at any time exceed $4,800,000,000
rows.explanation: The economics match: a $1.8bn increase on $3.0bn equals the CA's $4.8bn cap, and the $5m minimum per new lender is the same. The TS says the conditions for an increase are "Limited to" representations and no default, but the CA adds board resolutions, a legal opinion, testing of the conditions on the request date as well, a 30-day cut-off before maturity, and increases in integral multiples of $10m rather than a $10m minimum. Smaller differences: the limit is once per calendar year, and the Borrower Representative decides the allocation after consulting the Agent instead of deciding it jointly with the Agent. Because the CA caps total Commitments rather than the amount of increases, a borrower that has reduced its commitments could add more than $1.8bn in total. That point favours the borrower, but lenders never have to take part.

Mandatory prepayment applies if Aon UK Limited advances exceed 103% of the sublimit (s.2.7(b)). There is no cap on Aon Global Holdings plc or Aon Global Limited. If the TS cap was meant to cover all three TS-defined "UK Borrowers", the CA lets AGH and AGL draw beyond $1.0bn. The CA's own definition of "UK Borrower" covers all three UK entities, which makes the narrower AUK-only cap stand out. The TS wording is ambiguous, so the deal team should confirm.

rows.attribute: Benchmark rates, floors and credit spread adjustment
rows.ts_value: USD: Alternate Base Rate or Term SOFR. EUR: EURIBOR. GBP: SONIA, defined as the daily rate published on the fifth business day before the relevant day. No credit spread adjustment. Floors are not stated. ABR, Term SOFR and EURIBOR take their meaning from the Existing Revolving Credit Agreements.
rows.ts_quote: The interest rates shall not include a credit spread adjustment.
rows.ca_value: ABR is the highest of the Citibank base rate, Federal Funds Effective Rate + 0.5% and 1-month Term SOFR + 1%. Term SOFR has a Floor of 0.00%. The EURIBO Rate (Eurocurrency Base Rate) is floored at zero and grossed up for the Reserve Requirement. SONIA uses the fifth-Business-Day lookback and is floored at zero. The Federal Funds Effective Rate is floored at zero. No CSA; a spread adjustment appears only in the benchmark replacement provisions (s.2.23). ABR, the Term SOFR Rate, the Eurocurrency Rate and SONIA are defined as all-in rates that include the Applicable Margin.
rows.ca_quote: provided that if Term SOFR as so determined shall ever be less than the Floor, then Term SOFR shall be deemed to be equal to the Floor.
rows.ca_location: s.1.1 "Term SOFR" PDF p.29-30; "Floor" PDF p.20; "Eurocurrency Base Rate"/"Eurocurrency Rate" PDF p.18; "SONIA" PDF p.28; "Alternate Base Rate" PDF p.9; s.2.4 PDF p.35
rows.explanation: The benchmarks by currency, the absence of a CSA and the 5-business-day SONIA lookback all match. The CA adds 0% floors on every benchmark and a reserve gross-up on EURIBOR. The Term SOFR, EURIBOR and ABR floors may come from the Existing Revolving Credit Agreements, which were not provided. The SONIA floor cannot come from them, because the TS defines SONIA itself and gives it no floor.

For a split rating the higher rating applies, or one sub-grade below the higher if the gap is more than one sub-grade. Level V applies if there is no rating from Moody's or S&P. No initial pricing level is stated.
rows.ts_quote: As per the attached pricing grid, based on the Parent's long-term senior unsecured non-credit-enhanced debt ratings

The split-rating rule and the no-rating rule (Level V) are identical to the TS. Pricing changes as ratings change. No initial pricing level is stated.

rows.ts_value: Facility Fee per the grid (6.5-17.5 bps) on each lender's commitment regardless of usage. Paid quarterly in arrears on the last day of March, June, September and December and on the Commitment Termination Date. Calculated on a 360-day basis.
rows.ts_quote: payable on each Revolving Lender's commitment, irrespective of usage, quarterly in arrears on the last day of each March, June, September and December, and on the Commitment Termination Date. The Facility Fee will be calculated on a 360-day basis.

Paid on each Payment Date (last day of March, June, September and December) and on the Facility Termination Date. Calculated on actual days over a 360-day year (s.2.15). No fee accrues on a Defaulting Lender's unused Commitment (s.2.5). A Defaulting Lender earns the fee only on its funded Loans (s.2.21(a)(iii)).
rows.ca_quote: a facility fee at a per annum rate equal to the Applicable Facility Fee Rate on such Lender's Commitment from the Effective Date to the Facility Termination Date applicable to such Lender, payable on each Payment Date hereafter and on the Facility Termination Date applicable to such Lender
rows.ca_location: s.2.5, PDF p.36; s.1.1 "Payment Date", PDF p.24; s.2.15(a), PDF p.41; s.2.21(a)(iii), PDF p.46
rows.explanation: The rate, base, payment dates and day count all match. The CA adds customary Defaulting Lender rules that the TS does not mention: no facility fee accrues on a Defaulting Lender's unused Commitment.

rows.ts_value: Upon notice from the Agent or Required Lenders after a payment Event of Default, the Applicable Margin on overdue amounts increases by 200 bps per annum. Nothing applies automatically, and only overdue amounts are affected. Defaults continue until cured or waived.
rows.ts_quote: Upon notice from the Administrative Agent or the Required Lenders following the occurrence and during the continuance of any payment Event of Default, the Applicable Margin on overdue amounts will increase by 200 basis points per annum.
rows.ca_value: During a Default under s.7.2 (non-payment), the Agent or Required Lenders may by notice impose +2% on overdue Term SOFR, Eurocurrency, ABR and SONIA amounts. In addition, during an insolvency Default under s.7.6 or 7.7 (voluntary or involuntary insolvency of any Loan Party or Significant Subsidiary), the default rates apply automatically, without notice, to ALL Credit Extensions. "continue" means until cured or waived.
rows.ca_quote: provided that, during the continuance of a Default under Section 7.6 or 7.7, the interest rates set forth in clauses (a) through (c) above shall be applicable to all Credit Extensions without any election or action on the part of the Administrative Agent or any Lender.
rows.ca_location: s.2.11, PDF p.39; s.1.1 "Default", PDF p.15; s.1.1 "continue", PDF p.14; s.7.2, PDF p.78; s.7.6-7.7, PDF p.79; s.8.1(a), PDF p.80
rows.explanation: The payment-default rule matches (2% on overdue amounts after notice), and so does "continuing until cured or waived". The CA adds a trigger the TS does not have: an insolvency Default applies the 2% rate automatically to all outstanding Credit Extensions, not only overdue amounts. Sections 7.6 and 7.7 also cover the insolvency of any Significant Subsidiary, so the higher rate can apply even when the Obligations have not been accelerated. Automatic acceleration under s.8.1(a) applies only to US-organised Borrowers.

rows.ts_value: No amortization. All amounts are due in a single payment at the Commitment Termination Date. The TS states no mandatory prepayments.
rows.ts_quote: all amounts outstanding thereunder shall be payable in full
rows.ca_value: No amortization. All Obligations are due on the Facility Termination Date (s.2.2). Mandatory prepayment applies if, on a quarterly-or-more-frequent currency revaluation, total Advances exceed 103% of the Aggregate Commitment or Aon UK Limited Advances exceed 103% of the Aon UK Limited Sublimit. The excess must be repaid down to 100% within two Business Days of notice (s.2.7(b)). As drafted, limb (ii) adds all Dollar Advances to AUK's Committed Currency Advances.
rows.ca_quote: the Borrowers shall, as soon as practicable and in any event within two Business Days after receipt of such notice, prepay the outstanding principal amount of any Advances owing by the Borrowers
rows.explanation: The single payment at maturity matches. The CA adds a customary currency-fluctuation clean-down (a 103% trigger, repaid to 100%) that the TS does not state; the 3% headroom limits its effect. One drafting point should be confirmed: read literally, the AUK test in s.2.7(b)(i)(ii) counts all Dollar Advances to any Borrower, because "that are made to Aon UK Limited" follows only the Committed Currency part. That would force prepayments well beyond the TS sublimit. It is probably meant to count AUK Advances only.

rows.attribute: Optional prepayments, commitment reductions, minimum borrowing amounts
rows.ts_value: Commitment reduction: Parent may terminate or reduce unused commitments on at least 3 business days' notice, partial reductions at least $5m/GBP5m/EUR5m plus multiples of $1m/GBP1m/EUR1m, no reinstatement. Prepayment: no premium or penalty; same-day notice for Base Rate, 2 business days for Term Rate and 3 business days for SONIA; minimum $5m/GBP5m/EUR5m plus $1m/GBP1m/EUR1m increments; breakage costs on Term Rate Advances. Minimum Advance $5,000,000 plus $1,000,000 multiples (stated in dollars only). Advances are made ratably.
rows.ts_quote: The Parent will have the right, upon at least 3 business days' notice, to terminate or cancel, in whole or in part, the unused portion of the Facility Amount in excess of the aggregate outstanding Advances
rows.ts_location: PDF p.4, Commitment Reduction and Optional Prepayment; PDF p.3, Availability
rows.ca_value: Borrowers may permanently reduce the Aggregate Commitment in whole or in part (ratably) by at least $5,000,000 plus $1,000,000 multiples, on at least 3 Business Days' written notice, but not below Aggregate Outstanding Credit Exposure (s.2.5). Prepayments carry no premium or penalty: ABR same day by 11:00 a.m. NY time; Term SOFR 2 RFR Business Days; Eurocurrency 2 Business Days; SONIA 3 RFR Business Days. Minimums are the Borrowing Minimum and Borrowing Multiple, with funding indemnity under s.3.4 for Term SOFR and Eurocurrency (s.2.7(a)). Borrowing Minimum is $5m/GBP5m/EUR5m and Borrowing Multiple is $1m/GBP1m/EUR1m. An ABR Advance may be drawn for the full unused commitment. No more than 6 Term SOFR and 6 Eurocurrency Advances may be outstanding (s.2.6). Advances are made ratably (s.2.3).
rows.ca_quote: The Borrowers may permanently reduce the Aggregate Commitment in whole, or in part ratably among the Lenders in a minimum aggregate amount of $5,000,000 or any integral multiple of $1,000,000 in excess thereof, upon at least three (3) Business Days' written notice to the Administrative Agent
rows.ca_location: s.2.5, PDF p.36; s.2.6, PDF p.36; s.2.7(a), PDF p.36; s.2.3, PDF p.35; s.1.1 "Borrowing Minimum"/"Borrowing Multiple", PDF p.10-11
rows.explanation: Notice periods, minimums, increments, the no-premium rule, breakage and ratable funding all match. The CA differs only in mechanics: reductions are in USD only (commitments are USD-denominated), and the Borrowers rather than the Parent make reductions. ABR prepayments have an 11:00 a.m. same-day cut-off. Sterling and Euro minimum Advances are added. ABR draws can be below the minimum, and term-rate Advances are capped at 6 per type.

rows.attribute: Interest periods, notice periods and day count
rows.ts_value: Term Rates (Term SOFR, EURIBOR) have Interest Periods of 1, 3 or 6 months. Borrowing notice: same day for Base Rate if given before 12:00 p.m. NY time; 3 business days for Term Rate and SONIA. Interest is paid at the end of each Interest Period but at least quarterly for Term Rate, quarterly for Base Rate and monthly for SONIA. Day count is 365/366 for Base Rate and SONIA and 360 for Term Rate.
rows.ts_quote: Each Term Rate will be fixed for Interest Periods of 1, 3 or 6 months.
rows.ts_location: PDF p.5, Interest Rate and Interest Payments; PDF p.3, Availability
rows.ca_value: Interest Period of one, three or six months for Term SOFR and Eurocurrency. Borrowing Notice: 12:00 p.m. NY time on the Borrowing Date for ABR; 3 RFR Business Days for Term SOFR and SONIA; 3 Business Days for Eurocurrency (s.2.8). Interest is paid at the end of each Interest Period, every three months for longer periods, quarterly on Payment Dates for ABR and monthly in arrears for SONIA (s.2.15). Term SOFR, Eurocurrency and facility fees use a 360-day year; ABR and SONIA use a 365/366-day year.
rows.ca_quote: "Interest Period" means, with respect to a Term SOFR Advance or a Eurocurrency Advance, a period of one, three or six months
rows.ca_location: s.1.1 "Interest Period", PDF p.22; s.2.8, PDF p.37; s.2.15(a), PDF p.41
rows.explanation: Interest period tenors, notice periods, payment frequency and day counts all match. The CA counts SOFR and SONIA notices in RFR Business Days, which is a technical refinement.

rows.attribute: Term Rate Advances during an Event of Default (conversion/continuation restriction)
rows.ts_value: During a continuing Event of Default (after any cure period), each Term Rate Advance converts to a Base Rate Advance at the end of its current Interest Period.
rows.ts_quote: Upon the occurrence and during the continuance of any Event of Default (after giving effect to any applicable cure period), each Term Rate Advance will convert to a Base Rate Advance at the end of the Interest Period then in effect for such Term rate Advance.
rows.ca_value: While any Default (an Article VII event, i.e. an Event of Default) continues, no Advance may be made as, converted into or continued as a Term SOFR or Eurocurrency Advance unless the Agent and Required Lenders consent. At the end of the Interest Period, Term SOFR Advances convert automatically to ABR, and Eurocurrency Advances are exchanged into Dollars and converted to ABR (s.2.9).
rows.ca_quote: no Advance may be made as, converted into or continued as a Term SOFR Advance or Eurocurrency Advance (except with the consent of the Administrative Agent and the Required Lenders) when any Default has occurred and is continuing.
rows.ca_location: s.2.11, PDF p.39; s.2.9, PDF p.38; s.1.1 "Default", PDF p.15
rows.explanation: The trigger is the same: "Default" in the CA means an Event of Default, and the conversion happens at the end of the Interest Period in both. The CA also blocks new Term SOFR and Eurocurrency borrowings during a Default, which the TS does not address.

result.document_notes:
TS: \"Summary of the Revolving Facility\" (marked \"Posting Version\"), an 11-page lender-facing summary of terms for Aon North America, Inc., Aon Corporation, Aon Global Holdings plc, Aon Global Limited and Aon UK Limited. It is undated but refers to the merger agreement dated August 30, 2026, and it states that its terms are not final. Schedule I (Pricing Grid) is on PDF p.11. The TS also mentions a separate $4.0bn acquisition term loan under a different term sheet; that term loan is out of scope here.

CA: a new standalone Credit Agreement (Execution Version, filed as Exhibit 10.2) dated as of September 18, 2026. It is not an amendment. Parties are Aon plc (Parent/Guarantor), the five named Borrowers, Citibank, N.A. as Administrative Agent and BofA Securities as Syndication Agent. It is a $3.0bn multicurrency revolving facility. CA PDF page numbers are the printed page number plus 6.

Limitations:
(1) Schedule 1 (Commitments) only says \"[On File with Administrative Agent]\" (PDF p.136), so individual lender allocations cannot be reconciled. Only the $3.0bn aggregate can be checked.
(2) The fee letters dated August 30, 2026 referred to in CA s.4.1(h) and s.10.10 were not provided, so upfront and arrangement fee amounts cannot be checked.
(3) The TS takes the definitions of Alternate Base Rate, Term SOFR and EURIBOR from the Existing Revolving Credit Agreements, which were not provided.
(4) The pricing grids in both text files are garbled. Grid values were re-read with pdftotext -raw on TS PDF p.11 and CA PDF p.135, and all 15 values matched. Quotes for the grid rows are taken from the narrative text below each table.
(5) X01 is an extra TS interest term (conversion of Term Rate Advances during an Event of Default) that is not on the checklist.

All ts_quote and ca_quote strings were checked mechanically (whitespace collapsed) and appear verbatim in the text files.

Observations outside group A, for the other groups:
(a) The TS says \"each Borrower shall be a Guarantor\" (PDF p.2), but the CA \"Guarantor\" definition (PDF p.20) states that Aon UK Limited is not a Guarantor as of the Effective Date.
(b) The CA names HSBC, Morgan Stanley and Wells Fargo as additional Joint Lead Arrangers. The TS allows for \"any Additional Arranger\".
(c) The CA excludes Designated Subsidiaries organised in the EU, Iceland, Liechtenstein or Norway; the TS excludes only EU Member States.

rows.attribute: Financial covenants (type, level, step-ups, testing, cure rights)
rows.ts_value: (1) Interest cover (Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA to Consolidated Interest Expense) of at least 4.00x, tested quarterly from the first full fiscal quarter end after the Closing Date. (2) Leverage (Consolidated Funded Debt, net, to Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA), tested quarterly from the first quarter end after the Revolving Effective Date: maximum 3.50x before the Acquisition Closing Date; 4.75x in the closing quarter; 4.50x for full quarters 1-2; 4.25x for Q3; 4.00x for Q4-Q5; 3.75x for Q6-Q7; 3.50x from Q8. (3) Covenant reset: for acquisitions of $500m or more in a 12-month period, leverage rises to 4.00x for 4 quarters then 3.75x for 2 quarters, with a compliance certificate at 3.50x needed before another reset. (4) Netting of 65% of unrestricted cash plus Securities proceeds held for the Acquisition. No equity cure.
rows.ts_quote: commencing with the first full fiscal quarter end date occurring after the Closing Date, a ratio of Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA to Consolidated Interest Expense of not less than 4.00 to 1.00.
rows.ca_value: Interest cover of at least 4.0x, tested from the first Fiscal Quarter end on or after the Effective Date (s.6.14(a)). Leverage (s.6.14(b)) has the same levels and step-downs as the TS and is tested from the first Fiscal Quarter end on or after the Effective Date (TS: after the Revolving Effective Date; no practical difference because the agreement is dated September 18, 2026, which is not a quarter end). The reset mechanics are the same: $500m, 4.00x for 4 quarters then 3.75x for 2, compliance certificate at 3.50x. Netting covers 65% of Unrestricted Cash plus cash proceeds of Securities (defined as up to $13.5bn) not yet used but intended for the Acquisition. No equity cure.
rows.ca_quote: commencing with the first Fiscal Quarter end date occurring on or after the Effective Date, a ratio of Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA to Consolidated Interest Expense of not less than 4.0 to 1.0.
rows.ca_location: s.6.14(a)-(b) (PDF pp.75-76); s.1.1 'Consolidated Leverage Ratio' (PDF p.14), 'Securities' (PDF p.27), 'Unrestricted Cash' (PDF p.33)
rows.explanation: Levels, step-downs, reset and netting all match. The only drafting changes there are that the CA adds 'have not been used' to the proceeds netting, caps Securities at $13.5bn, and starts the leverage test 'on or after' rather than 'after' the effective date, with no practical effect. The real difference is the interest cover test: the CA starts it from the first quarter end on or after the Effective Date (likely September 30, 2026), whereas the TS starts it from the first full fiscal quarter end after the Closing Date (the term loan and Acquisition closing). This adds test dates before closing.

The mechanics differ in two ways. (1) KYC: the TS requires all KYC to reach the Arrangers at least 3 business days before the Revolving Effective Date, and a Beneficial Ownership Certification if requested at least 10 business days before. result.document_notes:
TS: "Summary of the Revolving Facility" (marked "Posting Version", undated; 11 PDF pages including the Schedule I pricing grid). It is a summary term sheet for a $3.0bn five-year revolving facility for Aon North America, Inc., Aon Corporation, Aon Global Holdings plc, Aon Global Limited and Aon UK Limited, with Aon plc as Parent. The facility is tied to the acquisition of USI Advantage Corp. under a merger agreement dated August 30, 2026, and to the refinancing of the 2021 and 2023 Existing Revolving Credit Agreements. Under its Documentation Principles, most legal terms only need to be "substantially similar/consistent" with the Existing Revolving Credit Agreements.

CA: a new, standalone Credit Agreement dated as of September 18, 2026 (Execution Version, filed as Exhibit 10.2; 161 PDF pages including exhibits and schedules). It is not an amendment, so the reconciliation is against this agreement as executed. The "Effective Date" is defined in s.4.1 as the date the conditions are satisfied, not as a fixed date. The agreement date and the September 18, 2031 Facility Termination Date are consistent with a September 18, 2026 Effective Date. In the CA body, PDF page numbers run 6 ahead of the printed page numbers (printed p.54 = PDF p.60). All page references here are PDF pages.

Limitations:
(1) Schedule 1 (Commitments) reads "[On File with Administrative Agent]" (PDF p.136), so individual lender allocations cannot be checked. Loan Party signature pages are PDF pp.111-112, and lender identities come from the lender signature pages, PDF pp.113-134.
(2) The Existing Revolving Credit Agreements were not provided. Items the TS fixes only by reference to them (assignments, yield protection, indemnity, related covenant definitions, basket sizes) are checked for consistency with the TS wording only, not against the existing agreements.
(3) The TS text extraction is two-column and garbled: on PDF pp.3-4, 6, 8 and 10 the heading labels are pulled out of line with their text. Headings were mapped to text by sequence. For example, on p.8 "Use of proceeds; merger; liens; affiliates; change in fiscal year; and indebtedness" is the Negative Covenants text, and on p.10 the two "substantially consistent" sentences are Yield Protection and Indemnity, in that order. Neither the original analyst nor the reviewer could render the PDFs as images to confirm this, because pdftoppm is not installed. The sequence mapping is consistent with the heading order on each page.
(4) The CA also contains standard provisions the TS does not mention: EU/UK bail-in (s.9.14), erroneous payments (s.10.12), lender ERISA representations (s.10.11), benchmark replacement (s.2.23), Disqualified Lenders (s.12.6) and a 20% cap on any one lender's commitment (s.12.2). These are noted where relevant, but because the TS does not state them they get no separate X rows.
(5) The reviewer added X12 (availability, borrowing mechanics and currencies) and X13 (voluntary commitment reductions). These are TS terms that are not on the Group A topic list; drop them if Group A already covers them.

Group A economic terms (amount, pricing, fees, maturity, accordion, extensions, sublimits, prepayments, interest mechanics, default interest and post-default rate conversion) are excluded under the task split.

rows.ca_value: Section 2.10: revolving loans are repaid at the Revolving Maturity Date. Swingline loans are repaid at the earlier of maturity and the 15th or last day of a month falling at least 2 Business Days after the loan is made. Section 2.11(b)(i): loans must be repaid or LC Exposure cash-collateralised if exposures exceed 100% of commitments (non-FX) or 105% (FX only), measured at the most recent Revaluation Date. Revaluation Dates are: borrowing, conversion and continuation dates; monthly for RFR loans; LC issuance and amendments that increase face amount; the first Business Day of each month for LCs; the last Business Day of each quarter; and any date the Agent picks while an Event of Default exists. The term-loan sweeps are struck (Section 2.11(b)(ii) is [Reserved]).

Providers are existing Lenders or institutions approved by the Agent (and, for a revolver, each Issuing Bank and the Swingline Lender), and each may decline. The facility is documented by a Refinancing Amendment executed by the Borrowers and the providing Lenders. Amendment No. 1 is itself such a Refinancing Amendment.

result.document_notes:
TS: 'Summary of Terms and Conditions' (a term sheet) for a $1,000 million Revolving Credit Facility for Michael Kors (USA), Inc., Capri Holdings Limited, Michael Kors (Europe) B.V., Michael Kors (Canada) Holdings Ltd. and Michael Kors (Switzerland) GmbH. It is marked 'Posting Version 6/5/2026' and runs 14 PDF pages, including Annex I (Interest and Certain Fees) and Annex I-A (pricing grid). Many TS terms simply refer back to the Existing Credit Agreement (the A&R Credit Agreement dated February 4, 2025).

CA: Amendment No. 1 dated June 24, 2026 (filed as Exhibit 10.1), a Refinancing Amendment under Section 2.27 that replaces the $1.5bn of existing revolving commitments with $1.0bn of 2026 Revolving Commitments (PDF pp.1-24). It attaches Exhibit A, a blackline of the A&R Credit Agreement 'Conformed through Amendment No. 1' (PDF pp.26-202). The reconciliation is against the agreement as amended.

Limitations:
(1) Exhibit A is a blackline, and the pdftotext output runs deleted and inserted text together (for example '$1,500,000,0001,000,000,000', 'July 1June 24, 20272031', 'Pricing Level 12' and the grid rows). Struck text was identified from the strike-through lines drawn in the PDF, using the read-only helper the first analyst left in the scratchpad (tools\pdfmark.py). In this review it was only re-run, printing to stdout; no files were created or changed. Some CA quotes therefore contain struck text, and each affected row explains this.
(2) Annex I (each lender's 2026 Revolving Commitment), Schedule 2.01(a), Schedule 2.02 (each Issuing Bank's LC commitment) and every schedule other than Schedule 1.01 are missing from the CA PDF. Lender allocations and LC commitments could not be checked.
(3) Where the TS says 'Same as the Existing Credit Agreement', CA provisions with no blackline changes were treated as matching. The Existing Credit Agreement itself was not provided separately.
(4) PDF page rendering was not available (pdftoppm is not installed). Neither pdftotext -layout nor -raw extracts the 'less than or equal to' symbols in the TS Annex I-A grid. The TS thresholds were read as upper bounds from the grid structure (Level 4 is '> 3.50:1.00'), and the CA grid's ≤ symbols were confirmed by the PDF strike parse.

Key findings:
(a) A12: the amendment deletes the Schedule 1.01 paragraph that defined 'Adjustment Date' and 'Pricing Level'. Section 1.01 still cross-refers to it, so the conformed CA does not say when grid pricing takes over from the initial Level 2 pricing. The TS ties the switch to the first compliance certificate. The unstruck 'Public Debt Rating' definition (PDF pp.73-74) also still contains ratings-based Pricing Level rules, although the grid no longer has a ratings column.
(b) A19: the CA allows 3-month Interest Periods in every currency and uses 365/366-day counts for GBP, JPY and CAD; the TS wording differs on both. Both differences are minor and favour the borrower.
(c) Minor mechanical differences in A04 (availability ends 'to but excluding' the maturity date), A14 (fronting fee base and timing) and A17 (LC revaluation dates).
(d) X01 was added for the TS 'Refinancing Facilities' term (CA Section 2.27).

rows.attribute: Financial covenants (type, level, step-ups, testing, cure rights)
rows.ts_value:
Covenant: maximum Net Leverage Ratio of 4.00x, tested at each fiscal quarter-end on a trailing four-quarter basis. Numerator: Consolidated Total Indebtedness plus capitalised Operating Lease Obligations, minus unrestricted cash up to $200m. Denominator: Consolidated EBITDAR.

Step-up: on a Transition Period Election after a Material Acquisition, the maximum is 4.50x 'for the four quarters following the Material Acquisition'. No more than two elections, with at least two full fiscal quarters between Transition Periods.

EBITDAR add-backs: extraordinary, non-recurring, unusual or exceptional items (with a matching deduction for such gains), and run-rate savings with an 18-month look-forward (12 months for cost synergies), capped at 15%.

No equity cure.
rows.ts_quote: the Net Leverage Ratio shall not be more than 4.50 to 1.00 for the four quarters following the Material Acquisition
rows.ts_location: PDF pp.7-8 - Financial Covenant (including Consolidated EBITDAR)
rows.ca_value:
Section 6.08: Net Leverage Ratio no greater than 4.00x at the end of each fiscal quarter. On a Transition Period Election for a Material Acquisition (consideration over $20m), the maximum is 4.50x during the Transition Period. Only two elections may be made, with two full consecutive quarters between Transition Periods.

The Transition Period runs from the first day of the fiscal quarter in which the acquisition closes to the last day of the fourth fiscal quarter after closing.

The Net Leverage Ratio definition matches the TS (cash netting cap $200m; Consolidated EBITDAR denominator). EBITDAR clause (a)(ix) adds back extraordinary items and (b)(v) deducts extraordinary gains. Clause (a)(x) allows run-rate savings over 18 months (12 months for synergies), capped at 15% of Consolidated EBITDAR.

No equity cure provision was found.
rows.ca_quote: the period commencing on (and including) the first day of the fiscal quarter during which Capri Holdings or any Subsidiary consummated such Material Acquisition and ending on (and including) the last day of the fourth fiscal quarter following such date of consummation

rows.explanation: The levels, the election limits, the ratio definition and the EBITDAR add-backs all match the TS. The Transition Period is longer than the TS's 'four quarters following': it includes the quarter in which the acquisition closes plus the next four, so 4.50x applies at five quarter-end tests.

rows.attribute: Required lenders, voting and sacred rights
rows.ts_value:
Required Lenders: more than 50% of revolving exposures, term loans and unused commitments.

Consent of each directly affected Lender needed for: increasing a commitment; reducing principal, interest or fees; postponing payments or commitment expiry; changing pro rata sharing; and subordinating liens or payment, unless each adversely affected Lender is offered the chance to provide the senior debt (excluding subordination already permitted, DIP financing and other customary exceptions).

100% consent needed for: changing voting percentages; releasing Capri, MK, or all or substantially all other Guarantors; releasing all or substantially all Collateral.
rows.ts_quote: Amendments and waivers with respect to the Credit Documentation shall require the approval of Lenders holding greater than 50% of revolving credit exposures
rows.ca_value:
Required Lenders: more than 50% of Revolving Credit Exposures, Term Loans and unused Commitments, excluding Defaulting Lenders.

Section 9.02(b) requires the consent of each affected Lender for commitment increases, reductions in principal, interest or fees, and postponements. Each Lender must consent to changes to pro rata sharing, voting percentages, and releases of Capri Holdings, the Company, or all or substantially all Guarantors. Carve-outs: changes to the Public Debt Rating definition, and default-interest waivers by Majority Facility Lenders.

Section 9.20 (Special Amendment Provisions): releasing all or substantially all Collateral needs each affected Lender, except as provided in s.9.14 or the Collateral Documents. Subordination of liens or payment is allowed only if each adversely affected Lender is offered a pro rata share on the same terms (offer open at least 10 Business Days). Subordination already permitted and DIP financing are excluded.

Section 9.02(d) allows replacement of Non-Consenting Lenders.
rows.ca_quote: release all or substantially all of the Collateral without the written consent of each affected Lender
rows.ca_location: s.1.01 'Required Lenders' (PDF p.78); s.9.02(b) (PDF p.181); s.9.20 Special Amendment Provisions (PDF pp.199-200)
rows.explanation: The Required Lenders threshold and the sacred rights match in substance. Small drafting differences: release of all or substantially all Collateral needs 'each affected Lender' rather than '100% of Lenders' (in practice the same here, with the s.9.14 collateral fall-away excepted); the Public Debt Rating and default-interest carve-outs are added; and the anti-subordination offer must stay open for 10 Business Days.

result.document_notes:
TS: 'Summary of Terms and Conditions' for a $1,000 million revolving credit facility for Michael Kors (USA), Inc., Capri Holdings Limited, Michael Kors (Europe) B.V., Michael Kors (Canada) Holdings Ltd. and Michael Kors (Switzerland) GmbH. It is marked 'Posting Version 6/5/2026', runs to 14 PDF pages and includes Annex I (interest and fees) and Annex I-A (pricing grid). For most terms it says they will be 'substantially the same as' the Existing Credit Agreement, the Amended and Restated Credit Agreement dated February 4, 2025. Its side headings do not line up with the paragraphs in the text extraction, especially on pages 4 and 6-10, so each paragraph was matched to its heading by order on the page.

CA: Amendment No. 1 dated June 24, 2026. It is a Refinancing Amendment under Section 2.27 of the A&R Credit Agreement dated February 4, 2025, with JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as Administrative Agent. Annex I replaces the existing revolving commitments with 2026 Revolving Commitments. The operative terms are in Exhibit A, a blackline 'Conformed through Amendment No. 1' that starts at PDF page 26. Each row was reconciled against the agreement as amended, meaning the Amendment No. 1 body plus Exhibit A.

Limitations and method:

(1) Exhibit A is a blackline. In the text extraction, deleted and inserted words run together, for example '$1,500,000,0001,000,000,000', 'March 3028, 20242026' and 'EBITDAREBITDA'. Deleted words that stand alone, such as 'Italy, ', are not marked at all. The page images could not be rendered because pdftoppm is not installed. Instead, the strike-through lines (about 2.4pt above the baseline) and underlines (about 1.8pt below it) were decoded from the vector drawing operators in the PDF content streams for the key pages: 33, 39, 42-46, 51, 58, 63-68, 73, 81, 83-84, 86-88, 141, 146, 150-154, 157, 160, 164-165, 167-168, 170, 181-182 and 199-200. Underlining also marks defined terms and words like 'provided', so not every underline is an insertion.

This decoding confirmed that deleted text comes before inserted text. It also found deletions the text does not show:
- Material Subsidiary and Secured Net Leverage Ratio now use Consolidated EBITDA instead of EBITDAR.
- Italy is deleted from 'IP Subsidiary', 'Eligible Jurisdiction' and the s.5.09(c) IP filing list, together with all Italian-law definitions and the Italian wording in Article VII(j).
- Former s.9.20 (Italian Transparency Rules) is deleted, and Special Amendment Provisions is renumbered from 9.21 to 9.20.
- The Initial USD and Euro Term Loan facilities are deleted throughout, so the Lenders are now only Revolving Lenders unless incremental term loans are added.
- The collateral fall-away and springback (s.5.09(d)-(g)) and the 'Investment Grade Rating' definition are new insertions.

(2) Annex I (each lender's commitment) and most schedules (1.01(b)-(d), 3.01, 3.06, 6.01, 6.02 and 6.04) are not in the extracted text. Only the pricing grid schedule is.

(3) The Existing Credit Agreement was not provided. Where the TS only says 'same as' or 'consistent with' it, the check confirms that the CA has a matching provision and, using the blackline, whether Amendment No. 1 changed it. It cannot confirm the original Existing CA wording.

(4) The cover page of Exhibit A still lists the 2025 titled agents. The 2026 roles are in the Amendment No. 1 recitals and the amended 'Lead Arrangers' and 'Co-Documentation Agents' definitions.

(5) Page references use the PDF page markers. The printed page numbers in the CA are different.

(6) All ts_quote and ca_quote values were checked mechanically against the text files, with whitespace collapsed. Some CA quotes (B01, B02, B05, X11) contain blackline-merged or struck words exactly as they appear in the extraction; the ca_value fields describe the text as amended.

result.document_notes:
TS: "Carnival Corporation and Carnival plc Revolving Credit Facility - Summary of Principal Terms and Conditions" (marked "Posting Version", "Restricted - External", undated, 14 PDF pages). It is a formal indicative term sheet for a $4bn senior unsecured multicurrency RCF, with JPMorgan as lead arranger and administrative agent. It includes Annex I (Interest and Certain Fees) and Annex I-B (pricing grid).

CA: a new standalone "Revolving Credit Agreement" (Execution Version), not an amendment. It is dated June 13, 2025 (Effective Date June 13, 2025) and is for $4,500,000,000 among Carnival Corporation (Lead Borrower), Carnival plc (Co-Borrower), the Subsidiary Guarantors, the Lenders and JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as Administrative Agent. It runs to 231 PDF pages, ending with signature pages. CA PDF page = printed page + 5.

Limitations:
(1) None of the listed Exhibits or Schedules is included. Schedule 2.01 (Commitments and Letter of Credit Commitments), Schedule 1.01(b) (Issuing Bank Sublimits) and Schedule 1.01(d) (Swingline Commitments) are missing, so per-lender commitments, per-issuer LC sublimits and swingline commitments cannot be checked.
(2) Fee letters (upfront, agency and any issuing-bank fronting fees) were not provided. Under s.10.09, only fee letters with the Administrative Agent, Arrangers and Joint Bookrunners survive.
(3) PDF page rendering was unavailable (pdftoppm not installed). The two pricing grids are garbled in the -layout text, so the reviewer re-checked them independently with pdftotext -raw on TS p.13 and CA p.66. All five tiers and all columns tie out.
(4) In the CA text file, the page numbers in the table of contents do not line up with the section headings (an extraction artifact). Some symbols (the 1/2 in the ABR definition, and the euro and pound signs) appear as replacement characters.

Drafting points found in the CA:
(a) 'Alternative Currency Sublimit' is used in s.2.09(f) but never defined.
(b) The 'Effective Date' definition cross-refers to s.4.01 rather than s.4.02 (the effectiveness conditions); the date is hard-coded, so this is harmless.
(c) The 'Applicable Margin' definition covers only Revolving Facility Loans, while the Pricing Grid applies a column to Swingline Loans.

rows.attribute: Letter of credit tenor, expiry, auto-renewal, reimbursement and lender participations
rows.ts_value: Each LC expires no later than the earlier of (a) one year after issuance, unless the applicable Issuing Bank consents, and (b) the fifth business day before final maturity. One-year LCs may auto-renew for one-year periods, but not beyond (b) unless cash collateralized or otherwise backstopped in a manner reasonably acceptable to the Issuing Bank. Drawings are reimbursed by the Borrowers on the next business day; if not, Lenders must reimburse the Issuing Bank pro rata. Each Issuing Bank has an LC sub-commitment and sole discretion above it.
rows.ts_quote: Each letter of credit shall expire not later than the earlier of (a) one year after its date of issuance unless consented to by the applicable Issuing Bank
rows.ts_location: PDF p.3-4, VI. Letters of Credit
rows.ca_value: s.2.05(c): each LC expires by the earlier of (i) one year after issuance (or extension), unless otherwise agreed by both the Administrative Agent and the applicable Issuing Bank, and (ii) five Business Days before the Revolving Facility Maturity Date. One-year LCs may auto-extend for periods of up to one year (not beyond (ii)) if the Issuing Bank can block extension once every twelve months. Expiry beyond (ii) needs the Issuing Bank's and Agent's sole-discretion consent, plus cash collateral of 102% of face for any such LC outstanding or issued within 30 days of maturity. Trade LCs expire by the earlier of 180 days and five Business Days before maturity. s.2.05(d): Lenders take automatic pro rata participations. s.2.05(e): the Borrowers reimburse by 2:00 p.m. on the next Business Day after notice, with an option to finance through an ABR Borrowing; unreimbursed amounts are funded by Lenders pro rata.
rows.ca_quote: Each Letter of Credit shall expire at or prior to the close of business on the earlier of (i) the date one year (unless otherwise agreed upon by the Administrative Agent and the applicable Issuing Bank in their sole discretion)
rows.explanation: The core tenor limits (one year; five business days before maturity), auto-renewal, next-business-day reimbursement and pro rata Lender participations match. The CA adds conditions the TS does not have: tenors over one year need the Administrative Agent's consent as well as the Issuing Bank's; LCs running past maturity need a fixed 102% cash collateral within 30 days of maturity instead of collateral or a backstop reasonably acceptable to the Issuing Bank; and the Issuing Bank must be able to block auto-extension each year. The CA also adds a 180-day trade LC limit.

Each Lender must buy a pro rata participation in each Swingline Loan, under certain circumstances, and fund its pro rata share on request.

'Swingline Loan': all Swingline Loans are in Dollars or Euros.

result.document_notes: TS: \"Carnival Corporation and Carnival plc Revolving Credit Facility - Summary of Principal Terms and Conditions\", marked \"Posting Version\" and \"Restricted - External\". It is undated and indicative, runs to 14 PDF pages, and includes Annex I (interest and fees) and Annex I-B (pricing grid). It describes a $4bn senior unsecured RCF; amount and pricing belong to group A. On PDF pp.3, 6 and 8 the two-column label/value layout is interleaved in the text extraction, and values were matched to labels by order. The Swingline, LC and Incremental blocks on p.3 are distinguishable by content; the p.6 and p.8 blocks follow the label order. CA: an executed new (not amended) $4,500,000,000 Revolving Credit Agreement dated June 13, 2025. Parties: Carnival Corporation (Lead Borrower), Carnival plc (Co-Borrower), the Subsidiary Guarantors, the Lenders, and JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as Administrative Agent and Global Coordinator. It runs to 231 PDF pages including signature pages (guarantors PDF pp.220-223, agent and lenders PDF pp.224-231); PDF page = printed page + 5. Limitations: (1) The Schedules (incl. 1.01(b) Issuing Bank Sublimits, 1.01(d) Swingline Commitments, 2.01 Commitments, 3.08(a) Guarantors) and Exhibits are listed in the CA but are not in the PDF or text. Guarantor identities were therefore confirmed from the signature pages, and lender commitments could not be checked. (2) The precedent documents named in the TS \"Documentation Principles\" were not provided: the Existing Revolving Facility, the 2020/2023 Term Loan Agreements and the Feb 28, 2025 Carnival Indenture Precedent. So \"substantially the same as\" or \"consistent with\" standards, and basket amounts, could not be verified against them. (3) Amount ($4bn TS vs $4.5bn CA), pricing, fees, LC/swingline sublimit amounts, facility currencies and the accordion belong to group A and are not reconciled here. Rows X16 (LC tenor and reimbursement mechanics) and X17 (swingline currency and mechanics) were added in review for TS terms covered by neither list. Every ts_quote and ca_quote was checked mechanically against the text files (whitespace collapsed) and found verbatim.

rows.attribute: Benchmark rates, floors and credit spread adjustment
rows.ts_value: ABR = highest of (i) WSJ Prime Rate, (ii) federal funds effective rate + 0.5% and (iii) one-month Term SOFR + 1.0%, with a 1.00% floor. Term SOFR (CME, set 2 U.S. Government Securities Business Days before the Interest Period) has a 0.0% floor. No credit spread adjustment. The TS says the rate provisions follow the Existing Credit Agreement and are only 'summarized in part'.
rows.ts_quote: "ABR" means the highest of (i) the rate of interest last quoted by The Wall Street Journal in the U.S. as the prime rate in effect (the "Prime Rate"), (ii) the federal funds effective rate from time to time plus 0.5%
rows.ts_location: PDF p.4-5 'Interest Rate Options' ('ABR', 'Term SOFR Rate')
rows.ca_value: Alternate Base Rate = greatest of (a) Prime Rate, (b) NYFRB Rate + 1/2 of 1% and (c) one-month Term SOFR + 1.00%, with a 1.00% floor. Term SOFR Rate has a 0.0% floor, and the initial Floor of 0.00% also applies to Daily Simple SOFR and any Benchmark Replacement. No credit spread adjustment. Section 2.09 sets the benchmark replacement mechanics.
rows.ca_quote: "Alternate Base Rate" shall mean, for any day, a rate per annum equal to the greatest of (a) the Prime Rate in effect on such day, (b) the NYFRB Rate in effect on such day plus
rows.ca_location: Section 1.01 'Alternate Base Rate' (PDF p.13), 'Floor' (PDF p.27), 'Term SOFR Rate' (PDF p.41); Section 2.09 (PDF p.56-58)

The CA uses the NYFRB Rate, which is the greater of the federal funds effective rate and the overnight bank funding rate, instead of the federal funds effective rate alone. TS: "Delta Air Lines, Inc. Revolving Credit Facility - Summary of Principal Terms and Conditions", marked POSTING VERSION / CONFIDENTIAL. It is a formal indicative term sheet: 11 pages of terms plus the Schedule I Pricing Grid on PDF p.12. It is undated but refers to a Commitment Letter dated May 6, 2026 and to no MAC since December 31, 2025. Several terms only say they follow the "Existing Credit Agreement" (the Amended and Restated Credit Agreement dated November 6, 2023): the Extension Option, the LC currencies, the interest rate provisions ("summarized in part") and the Refinancing Revolving Facilities. That agreement was not provided, so the CA terms that fill these in could not be checked against it.

CA: a new, standalone Credit Agreement dated as of June 11, 2026 (filed as Exhibit 10.4) among Delta Air Lines, Inc. as Borrower, the Lenders and JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as Administrative Agent. It refinances and replaces the Existing Credit Agreement in its entirety. It is not an amendment and has no conformed copy. The CA text runs to 128 PDF pages, with signature pages from PDF p.109. Schedules 2.01 (Commitment Amounts), 3.13 (Pacific Routes) and 6.05 (Pool Assets) and Exhibits A-D are listed in the index but are not in the file, so per-lender commitment allocations could not be reconciled. The Upfront Fee Letter and Administrative Agent Fee Letter (both dated May 6, 2026), which Sections 2.19 and 4.01(e) rely on, were not provided, so upfront fee amounts cannot be checked against the CA.

Pool Assets may be replaced dollar for dollar, or removed if the ACR is still met afterwards, in each case so long as no EoD exists or would result. There are no debt, restricted payment or investment covenants.
rows.ts_quote: so long as no event of default exists or would result therefrom, the Borrower shall be permitted to (i) replace a Pool Asset with any Additional Pool Assets
rows.ca_value: s.6.01 liens on Pool Assets: 8 categories of Permitted Liens, plus bans on value-impairing arrangements, assignment of sale proceeds and UCC/49 USC 44107 filings; s.6.01(b) double negative pledge. s.6.02: merger allowed if no Default and the survivor is the Borrower or a US-organised certificated air carrier that assumes the obligations; no liquidation. s.6.03 reserved. s.6.05 dispositions: Permitted Dispositions (including ordinary course and transactions under $50m FMV, subject to the ACR). A replacement needs only that no Event of Default exists, is dollar for dollar, and requires an Officer's Certificate and appraisal. A removal requires that no EoD exists or would result, plus ACR compliance on a fresh appraisal. No debt, restricted payment or investment covenants.
rows.ca_quote: so long as no Event of Default exists, the Borrower or any of its Subsidiaries may replace a Pool Asset with an Additional Pool Asset of the Borrower or any Subsidiary
rows.ca_location: Section 6 PDF pp.84-87 (s.6.01 pp.84-85; s.6.02 pp.85-86; s.6.05 p.87); "Permitted Disposition" PDF pp.35-36
rows.explanation: The covenant set matches; there is no debt, restricted payment or investment covenant in either document. The CA adds Permitted Disposition baskets, which the TS allows; its certificate and appraisal mechanics favour lenders but are procedural.

rows.attribute: Events of default and thresholds (cross-default, judgment, grace periods)
rows.ts_value: (1) principal or LC drawings not paid when due; (2) interest unpaid for 5 business days, or fees for 10; (3) other amounts unpaid for 10 business days; (4) misrepresentation, 30-day cure; (5) covenant breach, with customary cure for certain affirmative covenants and a 60-day ACR cure; (6) cross-payment default or cross-acceleration above $250m; (7) unsatisfied uninsured judgments above $250m in the aggregate, regardless of deductible; (8) bankruptcy of the Borrower or significant subsidiaries; (9) ERISA. Limited to these 9.
rows.ts_quote: 7. Unsatisfied judgments or orders not covered by insurance (regardless of any deductible and whether or not the insurer has been notified of such judgment or order) in excess of $250,000,000 in the aggregate.
rows.ts_location: PDF pp.9-10, E. Events of Default
rows.ca_value: s.7.01: (a) misrepresentation, 30-day cure after knowledge or notice; (b) interest 5 Business Days, fees and other amounts 10 Business Days, and principal, LC reimbursement obligations and LC cash collateralization when due (no grace); (c) Section 6 breach (including the FCCR) with no grace except the 6.04(a) cure; (d) other covenants, 30 days after knowledge or notice; (e) Material Indebtedness (Borrower Indebtedness above $250m in aggregate principal): payment default continuing 5 Business Days after any grace period, or acceleration, deemed cured if waived or cured by the holder; (f)-(h) bankruptcy of the Borrower or a Material Subsidiary (10% of assets/revenue, or any subsidiary holding Pool Assets), 60 days for involuntary cases; (j) Loan Documents cease to be valid; (k) any final judgment above $250m not covered by insurance and not stayed or bonded within 60 days; (l) ERISA Termination Event with MAE.
rows.ca_quote: any final judgment in excess of $250,000,000 (other than any judgment or order covered by insurance) shall be rendered against the Borrower or any of its Material Subsidiaries
rows.ca_location: s.7.01 PDF pp.87-89; "Material Indebtedness"/"Material Subsidiary" PDF p.32
rows.explanation: Payment, misrepresentation and covenant grace periods match. Judgment default: the TS threshold is $250m in the aggregate; the CA tests each final judgment separately (any final judgment above $250m), adds a 60-day stay/bond period and drops the TS wording 'regardless of any deductible and whether or not the insurer has been notified', which narrows the trigger (borrower favourable). Cross-default adds a further 5 Business Day grace, a waiver/cure rescission and counts only Borrower debt (borrower favourable). Against that, the CA adds an invalidity EoD (7.01(j)), makes failure to cash collateralize LCs when due an immediate payment default (not in TS item 1), and uses a Material Subsidiary test that captures Pool Asset holders (lender favourable).

rows.ca_value: Section 5. s.5.01: annual statements in 90 days, quarterly in 45 days, compliance certificate within those periods regardless of actual delivery, notices of ERISA and litigation events, plus Investment Property certificates and Pacific Route non-renewal notices. s.5.02-5.06: existence, insurance, properties, taxes, default notice. s.5.07: examination of books, records and appraisals and conferring with officers is limited to once a year absent an EoD (Borrower may join discussions); separately, the Agent and its agents (including appraisers) may visit properties and examine and monitor the Pool Assets 'at any reasonable time and from time to time' on reasonable notice, with no annual cap, at the Agent's expense unless an EoD is continuing; Pool Asset inspections are limited to visual walk-around of Aircraft. s.5.08 laws and sanctions. s.5.09 annual Appraisal Report (not in the year of the latest Termination Date). s.5.10 air carrier and citizenship. Appraisers: mba Aviation, BK Associates, ICF International, or others retained by the Agent and the Borrower. Separately, s.10.04(i) makes the Borrower reimburse Agent and Appraiser costs of periodic appraisals and other monitoring of Pool Assets.
rows.ca_quote: all reasonable fees and reasonable expenses of the Administrative Agent and the Appraisers incurred in connection with the Administrative Agent's (x) periodic appraisals and (y) other monitoring of Pool Assets as allowed hereunder
rows.ca_location: Section 5 (ss.5.01-5.10) PDF pp.81-84; s.5.07 PDF pp.83-84; "Appraisers" PDF p.15; s.10.04(i) PDF p.102
rows.explanation: The core covenants match, including the compliance-certificate timing and the annual appraisal. Two lender-favourable departures from TS item 6: (1) the TS caps visits, examinations and Pool Asset monitoring at once a year absent an EoD, but s.5.07 applies the annual cap only to book/record examinations and allows property visits and Pool Asset examinations and monitoring 'from time to time'; (2) s.10.04(i) shifts the cost of Agent and Appraiser monitoring and periodic appraisals to the Borrower, contrary to the TS rule (and s.5.07) that this is at the Agent's expense absent an EoD. result.document_notes: TS: "POSTING VERSION" Summary of Principal Terms and Conditions for the Delta Air Lines, Inc. Revolving Credit Facility. It runs to 12 PDF pages, including the Schedule I pricing grid. It is undated, but it refers to a Commitment Letter dated May 6, 2026 and a no-MAC date of December 31, 2025. CA: a new standalone Credit Agreement dated as of June 11, 2026 (SEC Exhibit 10.4 filing copy), not an amendment. It refinances and replaces the Amended and Restated Credit Agreement dated November 6, 2023 (the "Existing Credit Agreement"). The parties are Delta Air Lines, Inc. as Borrower, the Lenders, and JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as Administrative Agent, with 18 Joint Lead Arrangers/Bookrunners and 18 Co-Syndication Agents. Limitations: (1) Many TS terms (CPs, assignments, taxes, yield protection, bail-in, divisions, ERISA, erroneous payments, QFC, confidentiality, refinancing facilities) only say "Same as set forth in the Existing Credit Agreement". The Existing Credit Agreement was not provided, so those rows check that the CA contains the provision and that it is consistent and customary. They do not check it line by line against the prior agreement. (2) The TS pdftotext -layout file misaligns left-column labels against text on pages 4-6 and 10-11. Reading order was confirmed with pdftotext -raw: Governing Law = New York; Confidentiality = same as Existing Credit Agreement; Counsel = Simpson Thacher & Bartlett LLP. Page rendering of the PDFs was not available (also unavailable in the review pass). (3) Schedules 2.01, 3.13 and 6.05 were not reviewed for this group. (4) Group A economics (amounts, maturities, pricing, fees, accordion, extensions, prepayments, interest mechanics) are excluded here. Review pass: every ts_quote and ca_quote was checked mechanically against the text files (whitespace collapsed), and all were found verbatim. Section and page references were checked against the [PDF PAGE n] markers and are accurate. Corrections: X05 (the s.5.07 once-a-year cap covers only book/record examinations; property visits and Pool Asset monitoring are allowed 'from time to time', a further lender-favourable departure from TS affirmative covenant 6); B12 (the CA adds failure to cash-collateralise LCs when due as an immediate payment default, and the judgment EoD drops the TS deductible/insurer-notice wording); B09 (the 3.06(b) general compliance-with-laws rep and the 3.10 taxes rep extended to Material Subsidiaries go beyond the TS list); X07 (TS MAE limbs restated precisely). Added X15 (borrowing notice periods) and X16 (minimum borrowing amounts and the 20 Term Benchmark borrowing cap), which the TS states and which are not clearly group A topics.

result.document_notes: TS: a one-page lender presentation slide, not a formal term sheet. It is the "Executive Summary - Transaction Summary" page (deck page 14, PDF page 1). It describes a one-year extension and $1.0bn upsize of Duke Energy's existing $9.0bn Senior Unsecured Master Credit Facility to $10.0bn, with the existing maturity given as March 16, 2029. It carries no date and points to a separate "Summary of Terms", which was not provided. Both slide tables (Borrower Sublimits and Pricing Grid) are misaligned in the -layout text extraction. PDF page rendering is not available here (pdftoppm not installed), so their values were confirmed with xpdf pdftotext -table and -raw output (printed to stdout, no files written). Every sublimit, fee, all-in margin and borrower-tier mapping matched the first pass. Text quotes for these tables are the cleanest contiguous fragments in the -layout file. TS terms outside group A are not reconciled here: Arrangers, use of proceeds (general corporate purposes), and the financial covenant (Max Consolidated Debt/Capitalization 65.0%, or 70.0% for DUK and Piedmont), which belongs to the covenant group. CA: Amendment No. 2 and Consent dated March 14, 2025 (SEC Exhibit 10.1) to the Amended and Restated Credit Agreement dated March 18, 2022, which was previously amended by Amendment No. 1 dated March 17, 2023. Wells Fargo is Administrative Agent and Swingline Lender. Exhibit A is a conformed blackline, and its operative terms were reconciled as amended. Exhibit B replaces Schedule 1.01(a), the Commitment Schedule (27 Lenders totalling $10,000,000,000). LIMITATIONS: (1) The text file shows deleted (struck) and inserted (double-underlined) text side by side, old value first, e.g. "March 1716, 20282030" = March 16, 2030. The new Initial Sublimits total exactly $10.0bn and the cover changes $9bn to $10bn, which confirms the old-then-new order. The first pass reports confirming struck text from strike-through line objects in the PDF content stream: Base Rate floor 0% -> 1%; maturity March 17, 2028 -> March 16, 2030; per-Issuing Lender cap $40,000,000 -> $33,333,333; all ESG/Sustainability provisions deleted. This review could not repeat that check. Indirect evidence supports the ESG deletion: the TOC has no Section 2.20, and Section 7.05 has 'theirits' edits. (2) The blackline base maturity (March 17, 2028) differs from the TS existing maturity (March 16, 2029). This is consistent: the 2029 date came from a per-Lender extension under Section 2.01(b), and Recital B confirms the one-year extension to March 16, 2030. (3) The conformed copy leaves out the signature pages, Schedule 1.01(b) (Pricing Schedule), Schedule 1.01(c) and the Exhibits. The Applicable Margin, Facility Fee Rate and initial ratings-based pricing levels therefore cannot be checked against the CA. (4) Upfront fees sit in the fee letters dated February 20, 2025, which were not provided. Corrections made in this review: two page references (Section 3.02 is p.78; Section 2.11(a) is p.65), removal of an unsupported 'standby' LC description, an added note that the named Issuing Lenders' combined fronting caps (about $400m) sit below the $800m LC sublimit, and corrected TS table-source notes.

rows.ca_value: Defaulting Lender is defined by: a funding failure of 2 Domestic Business Days; notice of intent not to fund; failure to certify within 3 Domestic Business Days; or a Bankruptcy Event or Bail-In Action. Under 2.19 its facility fees stop, it is excluded from Required Lenders, its LC and swingline exposure is reallocated or cash collateralized within 2 Domestic Business Days, and a payment waterfall applies.
