result.document_notes:
TS: an undated 13-page "Marketing Term Sheet" from Truist Securities, Inc. for a $1,000,000,000 Senior Secured Revolving Credit Facility for Encompass Health Corporation. Pricing, fees and expenses are in Addendum I (PDF pp.10-13). It is marked "for discussion purposes only" and is not a commitment. Many terms (incremental, covenants, collateral, events of default) are set "substantially the same as the Precedent Credit Agreement" (the Sixth A&R Credit Agreement dated October 7, 2022, Barclays as agent). That precedent was not provided, so only the terms the TS states expressly could be reconciled.

CA: a new, standalone Credit Agreement dated as of March 9, 2026 (SEC Exhibit 10.1, 142 PDF pages) among Encompass Health Corporation, the Lenders, and Truist Bank as Administrative Agent and Collateral Agent. It is not an amendment, and the Closing Date is March 9, 2026.

Limitations:
(1) The filed CA ends with signature pages and does not include the Schedules (e.g. Schedule 2.01 Commitments, Schedule 2.05 Existing Letters of Credit) or the Exhibits. Individual lender allocations and existing LCs could not be checked; only the $1bn aggregate stated in the body was confirmed.
(2) The TS pricing grid (p.10) and the CA spread grid (p.9) are garbled in the -layout text. On review, both pages were re-extracted with pdftotext -raw to stdout, and every tier and column was confirmed. The less-than-or-equal symbols are dropped in both extractions, and tier boundaries were read from context. The grid quotes are the cleanest contiguous fragments of the layout text.
(3) In the TS's two-column layout, section headings are out of line with their text (for example, the "Maturity Date:" heading sits beside the LC and swingline sublimit text). Quotes were chosen so they do not run across those heading labels.

Review results: all ts_quote and ca_quote values were checked mechanically against the text files (whitespace collapsed) and all were found verbatim. Page references were checked against the PDF PAGE markers. Changes made:
- A08 was downgraded from match to match_minor_drafting, because CA 2.09(a)(iii) adds a 7-day Swingline repayment that the TS does not have.
- A14 was downgraded from match to match_minor_drafting, because the LC fee bases exclude unreimbursed LC Disbursements and the issuer fees are drafted as 'standard fees'.
- A15 and A16 locations were completed.
- X01 was added for the $3,500 assignment fee, which the first pass had left unreconciled.

Other economic items in the TS (covenant basket step-ups, Available Amount starter of $1bn, Significant Acquisition threshold of $100m, financial covenant levels) belong to other attribute groups and were not reconciled here. Spot checks confirmed the CA Available Amount starter of $1,000,000,000 (PDF p.12) and the Significant Acquisition threshold of $100,000,000 (PDF p.43).

rows.ca_value: Applies to each Borrowing and each LC issuance, amendment, renewal or extension. (a) Representations true in all material respects, with materiality-qualified reps true in all respects (no double materiality); (b) no Default at the time of and immediately after; (c) a Borrowing Request. The express LCT carve-out in s4.02 covers only Incremental Term Loans funding an LCT (reps limited to those the incremental lenders require; default condition limited to Specified Events of Default). The general LCT rule in s1.06(a) deems no-Default and rep conditions in 'any provision of this Agreement' satisfied if met at signing, at the Borrower's option.
rows.ca_quote: (b) at the time of and immediately after giving effect to such Borrowing or the issuance, amendment, renewal or extension of such Letter of Credit, as applicable, no Default shall have occurred and be continuing
rows.explanation: The three conditions and the no-double-materiality standard match, and dropping 'immediately prior to' is substantively equivalent. However, the TS applies customary LCT relief to clauses (b) and (c) for revolving credit extensions, while s4.02's express LCT carve-out is confined to Incremental Term Loans. Relief for a revolving draw funding an LCT depends on the general wording of s1.06(a), so it is less clear than the TS contemplated.

rows.attribute: Required lenders, voting and sacred rights
rows.ts_value: Required Lenders: more than 50% of loans and commitments. All or affected Lender consent is needed to: (i) extend or increase commitments or extend payment dates; (ii) reduce principal, rate (other than default rate) or fees; (iii) release all or substantially all Guarantors; (iv) release all or substantially all Collateral; (v) change voting percentages; (vi) change pro rata sharing of payments or commitment reductions; (vii) change the payment waterfall; (viii) subordinate the Agent's liens or the obligations.
rows.ts_quote: Amendments and waivers will require approval of Lenders holding more than 50% of the loans and commitments under the Senior Secured Revolving Credit Facility (the "Required Lenders")
rows.ca_value: Required Lenders: more than 50% of Combined Credit Exposures and unused Commitments, excluding Defaulting Lenders. Sacred rights: increase of commitment (that lender); reduction of principal, rate or fees, with financial-covenant and default-interest changes not counting as reductions; postponement of maturity, payment or commitment expiry; s2.18(b)/(c) pro rata sharing of payments and waterfall; voting provisions; release of all or substantially all guarantors or collateral (each Lender); class protection. Pro rata commitment reductions (s2.08(c)) are not on the sacred-rights list. Subordination of Obligations or Liens requires each directly and adversely affected Lender, but (a) only before a bankruptcy EoD under s7.01(g)/(h), and (b) Lenders offered a reasonable opportunity to participate pro rata in the new debt are deemed not affected. The CA also lets the Borrower, Required Lenders and Agent amend any provision if non-consenting Lenders' commitments are terminated and they are paid in full, and it disenfranchises Defaulting Lenders.
rows.ca_quote: provided, that, only those Lenders that have not been provided a reasonable opportunity, as determined in good faith by the Borrower in consultation with the Administrative Agent, to participate on a pro rata basis on the same terms in any new loans or other Indebtedness
rows.ca_location: §1.01 'Required Lenders', PDF p.41; §9.02(b), PDF pp.119-120; §2.08(c), PDF p.62
rows.explanation: The Required Lender threshold and most sacred rights match in substance. Sacred right (viii), anti-subordination, is narrowed in two ways: it does not apply after a bankruptcy EoD, and the Borrower can avoid lender-by-lender consent by offering all Lenders pro rata participation. This weakens the Serta-type protection the TS emphasised. Two further borrower-favourable gaps: the pro rata sharing protection covers only payments under s2.18(b)/(c), not commitment reductions (TS item (vi)), and the non-consenting lender payout mechanism lets Required Lenders override holdouts on any provision.

rows.ts_value: Assignments to banks, financial institutions and funds need Borrower and Agent consent, not unreasonably withheld. The Borrower is deemed to consent after 10 business days, and its consent is not needed during a payment or bankruptcy EoD. Minimum $5m, except for assignment of an entire commitment. No Borrower or Agent consent for assignments to a Lender, Lender affiliate or Lender-managed fund. $3,500 fee payable by the assigning Lender. Participations to banks and financial institutions need no consent, and the seller is not released.
rows.ts_quote: in minimum amounts of $5,000,000; provided that (i) no such consent of the Borrower or the Agent shall be required to any assignment by a Lender to another Lender, an affiliate of a Lender or to a fund managed by a Lender or an affiliate of a Lender
rows.ca_value: Borrower consent (deemed after 10 Business Days) is not needed for assignments to a Lender, Affiliate or Approved Fund, or during a Specified EoD (payment or bankruptcy). Agent consent is not needed for assignment of a Loan to a Lender, Affiliate or Approved Fund. Revolving Commitment assignments also need consent from the Swingline Lender and each Issuing Bank. Minimum $5m, with exceptions for assignments to Lenders or Affiliates and for whole-position assignments, and waivable with Borrower, Agent and Issuing Bank consent. $3,500 fee, payable with the Assignment and Assumption by 'the parties' and waived for assignments by or to Joint Bookrunners. Assignments to the Borrower or its affiliates, Defaulting Lenders, natural persons or Disqualified Institutions are prohibited. Participations need no consent, but not to Disqualified Institutions; the Lender's obligations are unchanged.
rows.ca_quote: (C) in the case of any assignment of a Revolving Commitment, the Swingline Lender and each Issuing Bank.
rows.ca_location: §9.04(b)-(c), PDF pp.123-127; 'Disqualified Institution' PDF p.22
rows.explanation: The core economics match: the $5m minimum, $3,500 fee, 10-business-day deemed consent and consent fall-away on payment or bankruptcy EoD. The CA adds an Issuing Bank and Swingline consent requirement and a Disqualified Institution blacklist, and narrows the Agent-consent exemption to 'Loans'. These are customary but are additional conditions not in the TS. Smaller mechanical differences: the minimum is also waived for assignments to Lenders or Affiliates, and the fee is payable by 'the parties' rather than the assigning Lender, with a Joint Bookrunner waiver.

result.document_notes:
TS: Truist Securities, Inc. "Marketing Term Sheet" for a $1,000,000,000 Senior Secured Revolving Credit Facility for Encompass Health Corporation. It is undated, runs to 13 PDF pages including Addendum I (Pricing, Fees and Expenses), and says it is for discussion purposes only and is not a commitment. Many terms are stated as "substantially the same as the Precedent Credit Agreement" (the Sixth A&R Credit Agreement dated October 7, 2022, with Barclays as agent), and only specific changes from that agreement are spelled out (basket upsizes, Available Amount starter, covenant levels, CPs, assignment and voting terms). The text layout interleaves left-column headings with body text (e.g. PDF pp.2-3, 8), so some contiguous phrases are broken by heading words in the extraction.

CA: a new standalone Credit Agreement dated as of March 9, 2026 among Encompass Health Corporation, the Lenders, and Truist Bank as Administrative Agent and Collateral Agent. It was filed as Exhibit 10.1 and runs to 142 PDF pages. Printed page numbers are 5 lower than PDF page numbers in the body. It is not an amendment: it replaces the Barclays-agented Existing Credit Agreement, whose payoff is a closing condition. Signature pages are included (PDF pp.138-142).

Limitations:
(1) The CA text stops at the signature pages, so none of the Schedules (e.g. 1.01A, 2.01 Commitments, 3.04, 5.18 Post-Closing Obligations, 6.02, 6.06) or Exhibits are in the file.
(2) The separate Collateral and Guarantee Agreement is not provided. Granular collateral scope, "Excluded Property" and the guarantee terms could only be checked through CA cross-references.
(3) The Precedent Credit Agreement is not provided. Where the TS says only "substantially the same as the Precedent Credit Agreement", the CA was checked against the specific terms the TS states, not against the precedent.
(4) Benchmark/index successor rate, the incremental facility (Permitted Incremental Amount of the greater of $1.4bn and 100% LTM EBITDA), sublimits, pricing, fees, default interest and day-count belong to Group A and are not repeated here.
(5) Pro forma calculation, the Available Amount and the bridge debt exception are folded into B07/B08 rather than given X rows, because those checklist items cover them.
(6) Review pass: all original quotes were verified verbatim against the text files. Corrections are mainly to explanations and page references (B06, B07, B11, B12, B14, B15, B16, X05, X07, X08, X16). Rows X17 (USD currency) and X18 (same-day Index Rate borrowing notice) were added.

rows.ca_value: Under new Section 5.15, if Total Revolving Extensions of Credit exceed $450,000,000 at any time, the Borrowers must deposit and maintain USD Cash Collateral of at least the Minimum Collateral Amount ($50,000,000 for Section 5.15). It is held in a segregated account at Citibank, N.A. under Agent control and earns no interest. The Borrowers must top up any shortfall promptly on the Agent's demand (Section 5.15(b)). The deposit is also a condition precedent to any credit event that takes exposure above $450m (Section 4.02(c)) and a Borrowing Limit (Section 2.01(e)). Release: on request, within 2 Business Days, once there is no Default or Event of Default and exposure has been below $450m for 3 consecutive Business Days. The account and control agreement must be in place by the earlier of 45 days after the Amendment No. 4 Effective Date (or a later date the Agent agrees) and any Borrowing Request above $450m. The definition of Total Liquidity expressly excludes Specified Cash Collateral, so the posted $50m does not count toward the minimum liquidity covenant.
rows.ca_quote: exceed $450,000,000, the Borrowers shall deposit and maintain Cash Collateral in United States Dollars in an amount not less than the applicable Minimum Collateral Amount
rows.ca_location: Exhibit A Section 5.15(a)-(d), PDF pp165-166; "Minimum Collateral Amount", PDF p72; "Specified Cash Collateral Release Trigger Event", PDF p88; "Total Liquidity", PDF p93; Section 4.02(c), PDF p152; Section 2.01(e), PDF p105
rows.explanation: The $50m amount and $450m threshold match. The CA fills in the release conditions the TS left open, as well as mechanics the TS left to the Agent's satisfaction. The CA terms are somewhat broader than a pure borrowing condition: the collateral must be maintained whenever exposure exceeds $450m (including through FX revaluation), with a top-up on demand; breach triggers mandatory prepayment through Borrowing Limit (e); the account must be set up within 45 days regardless of usage; and the collateral earns no interest. The CA also excludes the posted collateral from Total Liquidity. This fits the TS footnote, which counts only unrestricted cash as Liquidity, but it means posting the $50m reduces covenant liquidity. The TS's 'Total Revolving Credit Exposure' is called 'Total Revolving Extensions of Credit' in the CA.

result.document_notes:
TERM SHEET: this is not a formal term sheet. It is two Fluence Energy lender-presentation slides (deck pages 7-8, "Proposed Terms for Secured Revolving Credit Facility" and "(cont'd)", marked PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL). The slides are undated and show "Existing Terms" against "Proposed Terms" for an amendment to the $500MM senior secured revolver. In the pdftotext layout the row labels and the two value columns are interleaved, so the TS text file is garbled. The TS PDF could not be rendered in this environment (pdftoppm is not installed). The row mapping was therefore inferred from the order of the value columns. Slide 7 has 11 labels (Borrower, Guarantors, Security, Facility, LC Sublimit, Incremental, Maturity, Currencies, Pricing, SOFR Floor, Consent Fee) and 11 existing-term values in that order, with Borrower taking two entity lines. The Proposed column has 10 entries in order, Consent Fee having none. So the $50MM cash collateral proposal sits in the Facility row, and 'Reduce incremental capacity to $100 million' sits in the Incremental row. TS quotes are the cleanest contiguous fragments.

CREDIT AGREEMENT: Amendment Number Four to Syndicated Facility Agreement, dated March 31, 2026 (SEC Exhibit 10.1, Execution Version). It is among Fluence Energy, Inc. (Parent), Fluence Energy, LLC (Parent Borrower), Fluence Energy Global Production Operation, LLC, the foreign Guarantors, the Lenders and Citibank, N.A. as Agent. It comes with Schedule I (post-closing perfection actions, PDF pages 27-28) and Exhibit A (from PDF page 29), a conformed redline of the Syndicated Facility Agreement dated November 22, 2023 as amended by Amendments 1-4 (stricken and double-underlined text). The reconciliation is against the agreement as amended by Amendment No. 4.

LIMITATIONS:
(1) The text extraction merges stricken and inserted words, for example "20252026", "20262027", "andplus", "CollateralAdministrative" and "ifmade". CA pages could not be rendered. Redline status was read from strike and underline line segments in the PDF content streams, using a read-only helper script in the session scratchpad (tools\redline.py). This review spot-checked the 6.01(e) proviso (underline confirms the inserted '(A) prior to the Trigger Date such Indebtedness is unsecured and (B) from and after the Trigger Date,') and the 6.09(k) run containing '1.101%'. Some CA quotes contain merged deleted and inserted text exactly as it appears in the file; the explanations give the operative reading.
(2) The CA does not set out the 10 bps consent fee (probably in a separate fee letter). Schedules such as Schedule 2.01 (Commitments/Issuing Banks) were not reconciled.
(3) Group A items on the slides were left to the other analyst: facility amount, LC sublimit/cash draw sublimit, incremental reduction to $100MM, maturity, pricing and SOFR floor. Currencies is not on the Group A topic list and is reconciled here as X13.
(4) All ts_quote and ca_quote values were checked mechanically (whitespace collapsed) against the text files, and all were found.

rows.explanation: The core capacity matches: a $535M / 100% EBITDA fixed amount plus unlimited capacity at secured leverage of 1.25x or less, with $20M/$5M minimums and sublimit consent protections. The terms differ in substance in both directions. In the Borrowers' favour, the CA adds increases to the existing term tranche, deducts from the fixed amount only usage in reliance on it (with automatic reclassification to the ratio basket; the TS deducted all prior Incremental Facilities), adds LCA carve-outs, tests the no-default condition only at effectiveness (the TS also tested at request) and allows junior-ranking IED where the TS required pari passu. In the lenders' favour, the CA adds a rep bring-down, pro forma financial covenant compliance and WAL tests that the TS did not state. On balance the Borrowers gain flexibility. All of the changes are customary, so the difference is minor.

rows.ts_value: $150,000,000 standby LC sublimit within the RC, covering performance and financial LCs, with financial LCs capped at $75,000,000. Bank of America issues as Fronting Bank. LCs can be issued from the Closing Date to the Maturity Date. If an FX recalculation pushes LC exposure above 105% of the $150M sublimit, the Borrowers must cash collateralise the amount needed to eliminate that excess.
rows.ts_quote: an amount equal to 105% of the sublimit of $150,000,000 for Letters of Credit, the Borrowers will cash collateralize Letters of Credit in the amount necessary to eliminate such excess.
rows.ts_location: PDF p.2 (Senior Credit Facility); PDF p.3 (105% cash collateral); PDF pp.5-6 (Availability - LC issuance to Maturity Date)
rows.ca_value: The Letter of Credit Sublimit is the lesser of the RC Facility and $150,000,000, and sits within the RC. Financial Letter of Credit Sublimit: $75,000,000. Letters of Credit are standby only. The L/C Issuer is Bank of America ($150,000,000 L/C Commitment under Schedule 2.01), plus up to three additional Lenders the Company may select. LCs can be issued until the Letter of Credit Expiration Date, seven days before the Maturity Date. Each LC must be at least the Dollar Equivalent of $1,000,000 (unless otherwise agreed) and expire within twelve months unless the Required Revolving Lenders approve. Under s.2.05(d), if outstanding LCs exceed 105% of the sublimit 'as a result of fluctuations in exchange rates or for any other reason', the Borrowers must, within two Business Days, cash collateralise enough to bring the Outstanding Amount down to 100% of the sublimit.
rows.ca_quote: 105% of the Letter of Credit Sublimit then in effect, then, within two Business Days after receipt of such notice, the Borrowers shall Cash Collateralize L/C Obligations in an aggregate amount sufficient to reduce such Outstanding Amount as of such date of payment to an amount not to exceed 100%
rows.ca_location: s.1.01 'L/C Issuer', 'Letter of Credit', 'Letter of Credit Expiration Date', 'Letter of Credit Sublimit' (PDF p.15); s.2.03(a) (PDF pp.27-28); s.2.05(d) (PDF p.34); Schedule 2.01 (PDF p.84)
rows.explanation: The $150M sublimit, the $75M financial LC cap, standby-only LCs and Bank of America as issuer match. The differences are: (1) the TS requires cash collateral only for the excess over 105% of the sublimit and only after an FX recalculation; the CA applies the 105% trigger to any cause and requires cash collateral down to 100%, so a breach costs the Borrowers up to $7.5M (5% of the sublimit) more in cash collateral; (2) issuance stops seven days before the Maturity Date, not at the Maturity Date; (3) the CA adds a $1M minimum LC amount and a twelve-month tenor cap. These favour the lenders. Against them, the CA lets the Company add up to three additional L/C Issuers, where the TS named only Bank of America, which favours the Borrowers. Overall this is a minor difference in the lenders' favour.

rows.ts_value: $20,000,000 swingline sublimit. Bank of America is Swingline Lender at its sole discretion, in USD only, same day, with a $1,000,000 minimum. Each Swingline Loan must be repaid within ten business days. Swingline Loans bear interest at the Base Rate plus the Base Rate margin.
rows.ts_quote: in its sole discretion, on a same day basis in an aggregate amount not exceeding $20,000,000 and in minimum amounts of $1,000,000. The Borrowers must repay each Swingline Loan in full no later than ten (10) business days after such loan is made.
rows.ts_location: PDF p.2 (Swingline Option); PDF p.14 (Interest Rates)
rows.ca_value: The Swing Line Sublimit is the lesser of $20,000,000 and the RC Facility. Bank of America may, at its sole discretion, make Swing Line Loans in Dollars to the Company. Notice is due by 10:00 a.m. on the borrowing date, with a $1,000,000 minimum. Repayment is due on the earlier of ten Business Days after the loan is made and the Maturity Date. Swing Line Loans are Base Rate Loans at the Base Rate plus the RC Applicable Rate.
rows.ca_quote: means, at any time, an amount equal to the lesser of (a) $20,000,000 and (b) the Revolving Credit Facility.
rows.ca_location: s.1.01 'Swing Line Sublimit' (PDF p.21); s.2.04(a)-(b) (PDF pp.32-33); s.2.07(b) and s.2.08(a)(iii) (PDF p.35)
rows.explanation: Amount, discretion, minimum, ten-business-day repayment and Base Rate pricing all match. The CA makes Swing Line Loans available to the Company specifically, a drafting refinement of the TS reference to 'the Borrowers'.

rows.ts_value: No borrower-specific sublimits. There is a $75,000,000 cap on financial letters of credit within the $150M LC sublimit.
rows.ts_quote: however up to $75,000,000 only can be utilized for the issuance of financial letters of credit
rows.ca_value: Financial Letter of Credit Sublimit of $75,000,000, within the Letter of Credit Sublimit. There are no borrower-specific or Alternative Currency sublimits. The $75,000,000 cap on delayed-draw Term Loans is covered in A01/A02.
rows.ca_quote: means an amount equal to $75,000,000. The Financial Letter of Credit Sublimit is part of, and not in addition to, the Letter of Credit Sublimit.
rows.ca_location: s.1.01 'Financial Letter of Credit Sublimit' (PDF p.11); s.2.03(a)(i) (PDF p.27)
rows.explanation: The $75M financial LC sub-sublimit is the same in both documents. Neither document has borrower-level sublimits.

rows.attribute: Benchmark rates, floors and credit spread adjustment
rows.ts_value: The Benchmark Rate is Term SOFR (the forward-looking term rate published two U.S. government securities business days before the interest period). The Base Rate is the highest of BofA prime, Fed Funds + 0.50% and Benchmark Rate + 1.00%. Both the Benchmark Rate and the Base Rate are floored at zero. The existing SOFR Adjustment (credit spread adjustment) is removed.
rows.ts_quote: Notwithstanding the foregoing, in no event shall the Benchmark Rate or the Base Rate be less than zero.
rows.ts_location: PDF p.14 (Addendum I - Interest Rates; SOFR Adjustment)
rows.ca_value: Term SOFR is the CME Term SOFR Screen Rate two U.S. Government Securities Business Days before the Interest Period, floored at zero. The Base Rate is the highest of Fed Funds + 1/2 of 1%, BofA prime rate, Term SOFR + 1.00%, and 1.00%. The Federal Funds Rate is floored at zero. No SOFR Adjustment or credit spread adjustment appears anywhere in the CA.
rows.ca_quote: the highest of (a) the Federal Funds Rate plus 1/2 of 1%, (b) the rate of interest in effect for such day as publicly announced from time to time by Bank of America as its "prime rate", (c) Term SOFR plus 1.00%, and (d) 1.00%.
rows.ca_location: s.1.01 'Base Rate' (PDF p.5); 'Federal Funds Rate' (PDF p.11); 'Term SOFR' (PDF p.22)
rows.explanation: The Term SOFR benchmark, its zero floor and the removal of the CSA all match. The CA adds a 1.00% floor to the Base Rate, where the TS only floored it at zero. This favours lenders but has little practical effect while the prime rate is well above 1%.

rows.attribute: Applicable margin / pricing grid (check EVERY tier and EVERY column)
rows.ts_value: Grid in bps by Leverage Ratio, columns in the order commitment fee / Term SOFR and Financial LC / Performance LC / Base Rate (including Swingline). L1 <1.50x: 17.5 / 125.0 / 83.3 / 25.0. L2 1.50x: 20.0 / 150.0 / 100.0 / 50.0. L3 2.00x: 25.0 / 162.5 / 105.0 / 62.5. L4 2.50x: 30.0 / 175.0 / 120.0 / 75.0. L5 3.25x: 35.0 / 200.0 / 135.0 / 100.0. One grid covers the whole Senior Credit Facility (RC and Term).
rows.ts_quote: and the Applicable Margin for Base Rate loans shall be the applicable rate per annum set forth in the table below opposite the Leverage Ratio determined as of the last day of the immediately preceding fiscal quarter.
rows.ts_location: PDF p.15 (Addendum I - Performance Pricing grid)
rows.ca_value: RC grid by Consolidated Leverage Ratio, columns in the order Commitment Fee / Term SOFR and Financial LC Fee / Performance LC Fee / Base Rate. L1 <1.50: 0.175% / 1.250% / 0.833% / 0.250%. L2 >=1.50 and <2.00: 0.200% / 1.500% / 1.000% / 0.500%. L3 >=2.00 and <2.50: 0.250% / 1.625% / 1.050% / 0.625%. L4 >=2.50 and <3.25: 0.300% / 1.750% / 1.200% / 0.750%. L5 >=3.25: 0.350% / 2.000% / 1.350% / 1.000%. rows.ca_quote: 1 Less than 1.50 to 1.00 0.175% 1.250% 0.833% 0.250% 2 Greater than or equal to 1.50 to 1.00 but less than 2.00 to 1.00 0.200% 1.500% 1.000% 0.500% 3 Greater than or equal to 2.00 to 1.00 but less than 2.50 to 1.00 0.250% 1.625% 1.050% 0.625%
rows.ca_location: s.1.01 'Applicable Rate' (PDF p.4)
rows.explanation: All 5 tiers and all 4 TS columns match exactly once bps are converted to %, for both the RC and Term grids. The TS shows only lower bounds (<1.50x, 1.50x, 2.00x, 2.50x, 3.25x), which correspond to the CA ranges. The TS grid is garbled in the layout text, so the TS quote is the clean lead-in sentence and the values come from a raw-mode extraction of TS PDF p.15. The Term Facility ticking fee column is covered in A15.

rows.attribute: Pricing basis (ratings / leverage / flat) and initial pricing level
rows.ts_value: Pricing is based on the Leverage Ratio (consolidated funded debt / Consolidated EBITDA) at the end of the prior fiscal quarter. Pricing Level 4 applies from the Closing Date until the first business day after the compliance certificate for the quarter ending March 31, 2026 is delivered.
rows.ts_quote: in effect from the Closing Date through the first business day immediately following the date a compliance certificate calculating the Leverage Ratio as of the fiscal quarter ending March 31, 2026 is delivered to the Administrative Agent shall be determined based upon Pricing Level 4
rows.ts_location: PDF p.10 (Leverage Ratio definition); PDF p.14 (Addendum I - Interest Rates); PDF p.15 (Performance Pricing)
rows.ca_value: Pricing is based on the Consolidated Leverage Ratio (Consolidated Funded Indebtedness / Consolidated EBITDA). Pricing Level 4 applies to both the RC and Term Facility until the first Business Day after the Q1 2026 Compliance Certificate is delivered. After that, pricing follows the most recent Compliance Certificate, effective the first Business Day after delivery. If a Compliance Certificate is late, Pricing Level 5 applies at the Required Lenders' request. Pricing is adjusted retroactively if the ratio was miscalculated (s.2.10(b)).
rows.ca_quote: (i) for the Revolving Credit Facility, from the Closing Date to the first Business Day immediately following the date of delivery (the "Revolving Delivery Date") of the Compliance Certificate for the fiscal quarter ending March 31, 2026, the following percentages per annum based on Pricing Level 4
rows.ca_location: s.1.01 'Applicable Rate' (PDF pp.4-5); 'Consolidated Leverage Ratio' (PDF p.8); s.2.10(b) (PDF p.36)
rows.explanation: Leverage-based pricing and the initial Level 4 through the Q1 2026 compliance certificate match. The CA adds pricing protections that the TS does not have. Level 5 applies, at the Required Lenders' request, while a Compliance Certificate is overdue, and s.2.10(b) requires retroactive payment if the ratio was misstated. Because these change pricing outcomes, they are a difference rather than drafting. They are customary, so the difference is minor and favours the lenders.

rows.ts_value: Commitment fee at the grid rate (17.5-35.0 bps by Leverage Ratio) on the actual daily unused RC. Payable quarterly in arrears from the first quarterly payment date after closing. Swingline Loans do not count as utilisation.
rows.ts_quote: a commitment fee of a percentage per annum determined in accordance with the pricing grid set forth below, based on the Leverage Ratio, shall be payable on the actual daily unused portions of the Revolving Credit Facility
rows.ca_value: Applicable Rate (0.175%-0.350%) times the actual daily amount by which the RC Facility exceeds outstanding RC Loans plus L/C Obligations. Swing Line Loans do not count as usage. Payable quarterly in arrears on the last Business Day of March, June, September and December, starting with the first such date after closing, and at the end of the Availability Period.
rows.ca_quote: a commitment fee in Dollars equal to the Applicable Rate times the actual daily amount by which the Revolving Credit Facility exceeds the sum of (i) the Outstanding Amount of Revolving Credit Loans and (ii) the Outstanding Amount of L/C Obligations
rows.explanation: Rate grid, unused-amount base, exclusion of swingline usage and quarterly payment in arrears all match.

rows.attribute: Letter of credit participation fee and fronting fee
rows.ts_value: Financial LC fee equals the Term SOFR margin (125-200 bps). Performance LC fee runs from 83.3 to 135 bps. Both are charged on the maximum amount available to be drawn, paid quarterly in arrears and shared pro rata among RC Lenders. A fronting fee is payable to the Fronting Bank in the amount set out in the Fee Letter.
rows.ts_quote: with respect to financial Letters of Credit, at a rate per annum equal to the financial Letter of Credit fee as set forth in the pricing grid below, and (ii) with respect to performance Letters of Credit, at a rate per annum equal to the performance Letter of Credit fee
rows.ts_location: PDF pp.14-15 (Addendum I - Letter of Credit Fees)
rows.ca_value: Performance and Financial LC Fees are charged at the respective Applicable Rates on the daily amount available to be drawn, with automatic increases counted at their maximum under s.1.09. They are payable quarterly in arrears on the first Business Day after each quarter end and are shared by Applicable Percentage. During an Event of Default they accrue at the Default Rate on the Required Lenders' request. The fronting fee is at a rate separately agreed between the Borrower and the L/C Issuer, payable on the 10th Business Day after each quarter end, plus customary processing charges.
rows.ca_quote: (i) for each Performance Letter of Credit equal to the Applicable Rate (for Performance Letters of Credit) times the Dollar Equivalent of the daily amount available to be drawn under each such Performance Letter of Credit
rows.explanation: The LC fee rates and the financial/performance split match the grid. Differences are only in payment mechanics. The fronting fee amount appears in neither document (it sits in the Fee Letter or a separate agreement, not provided).

rows.attribute: Upfront, ticking, term-out, extension or other fees stated in the TS
rows.ts_value: The TS states only a fronting fee (amount in the Fee Letter) and a $3,500 assignment fee. It states no upfront, ticking, term-out or extension fees; the Term Loan is fully drawn at closing.
rows.ts_quote: In addition, a fronting fee shall be payable to the Fronting Bank for its own account, in an amount set forth in the Fee Letter.
rows.ts_location: PDF p.15 (Addendum I - Letter of Credit Fees); PDF p.11 (Assignments Generally)
rows.ca_value: New ticking fee under s.2.09(a)(ii) on unused Term Commitments at the Term grid rate (0.175%-0.350%; 0.300% at the initial Level 4). It accrues from October 4, 2025 through the Term Availability Period and is payable quarterly. Arranger and Agent fees follow the Fee Letters (Fee Letter dated June 30, 2025) under s.2.09(b). A $3,500 assignment processing fee applies under s.10.06(b)(iv). The fronting fee is set by separate agreement.
rows.ca_quote: a ticking fee in Dollars equal to the Applicable Rate times the actual daily amount by which the Term Facility exceeds the Outstanding Amount of Term Loans, subject to adjustment as provided in Section 2.16. The ticking fee shall accrue beginning on (and including) October 4, 2025
rows.ca_location: s.2.09(a)(ii), (b) (PDF p.36); s.1.01 'Fee Letter' (PDF p.11); s.10.06(b)(iv) (PDF p.76)
rows.explanation: The ticking fee is not in the TS. It comes from the CA's delayed-draw term feature (A01/A02). Exposure is small: at most $75M undrawn for about four months at 17.5-35 bps. The $3,500 assignment fee matches. Fee Letter amounts could not be reconciled because the Fee Letter was not provided.

rows.ts_value: While any default continues, the margin on obligations rises by 2% a year. This is automatic for a principal payment default and otherwise applies only at the Required Lenders' request.
rows.ts_quote: the Applicable Margin on obligations owing under the loan documentation for the Senior Credit Facility shall increase by 2% per annum (subject, in all cases other than a default in the payment of principal when due, to the request of the Required Lenders)
rows.ca_value: The Default Rate is the Base Rate plus the Base Rate Applicable Rate plus 2%. For Term SOFR Loans it is the applicable rate plus 2%, and for LC Fees the Applicable Rate plus 2%. Overdue principal bears the Default Rate automatically. Other overdue amounts bear it at the Required Lenders' request. While any Event of Default exists, all Obligations bear it at the Required Lenders' request after written notice to the Company. LC Fees bear it during an Event of Default at the Required Lenders' request.
rows.ca_quote: Upon the request of the Required Lenders and after written notice to the Company, while any Event of Default exists (other than as set forth in clauses (b)(i) and (b)(ii) above), the Borrowers shall pay interest on the principal amount of all outstanding Obligations hereunder
rows.ca_location: s.1.01 'Default Rate' (PDF p.9); s.2.08(b) (PDF p.35); s.2.03(h) (PDF p.31)
rows.explanation: The +2% step-up and the split between automatic (principal) and Required Lenders' request match. The CA narrows the TS mechanic, though. Under the TS, a principal payment default automatically raises the margin on all obligations. Under the CA, only the overdue principal bears the Default Rate automatically, and the step-up on all Obligations needs a Required Lenders' request and written notice to the Company while an Event of Default exists. The narrower trigger and added notice condition are a minor difference in the Borrowers' favour.

rows.ts_value: Quarterly Term Loan amortization as a % of the original stated amount: 0.000% per quarter from Q/E 12/31/2025 to 9/30/2026, 0.625% per quarter from 12/31/2026 to 9/30/2027, and 1.250% per quarter thereafter, with the balance due at maturity. The only mandatory prepayment trigger is LC cash collateralisation of the excess if an FX recalculation moves exposure above 105% of the sublimit. There are no asset sale or debt sweeps.
rows.ts_quote: Beginning with the first full fiscal quarter ending after the Closing Date, the Term Loan Facility will be subject to quarterly amortization based upon the percentages of the original stated amount of the Term Loan Facility set forth below, with the remainder being due on the Maturity Date.
rows.ts_location: PDF p.5 (Scheduled Amortization); PDF p.3 (105% LC cash collateral)
rows.ca_value: s.2.07(c) uses the same percentages of the initial principal amount of the Term Loans, starting with the quarter ending 12/31/2025, with the balance due on the Maturity Date. Mandatory prepayments: s.2.05(c) requires prepayment or cash collateral within two Business Days if Total Revolving Credit Outstandings exceed the RC Commitments. s.2.05(d) requires LC cash collateral within two Business Days if LC exposure exceeds 105% of the LC Sublimit for FX or any other reason, enough to bring exposure down to 100% of the sublimit. There are no asset sale, debt issuance or ECF sweeps.
rows.ca_quote: Each fiscal quarter commencing with the quarter ending December 31, 2025, to (and including) September 30, 2026 0.000% Each fiscal quarter commencing with the quarter ending December 31, 2026, to (and including) September 30, 2027 0.625% Each fiscal quarter thereafter 1.250%
rows.explanation: The amortization schedule matches exactly (0.000% / 0.625% / 1.250% per quarter, starting with the first full quarter after closing). Mandatory prepayments differ. The CA adds a customary RC overadvance prepayment that the TS does not state. Its 105% LC trigger also applies for any reason and requires cash collateral down to 100% of the sublimit, where the TS required only the excess over 105% (see A07). Both changes favour the lenders and are minor. Because the percentages apply to the upsized $675M Term Facility, the dollar instalments are higher than under the TS (see A02).

rows.attribute: Optional prepayments, commitment reductions, minimum borrowing amounts
rows.ts_value: The facility can be prepaid in whole or part at any time without premium or penalty, subject to breakage. Unused RC commitments can be irrevocably reduced or terminated at any time without penalty. The only stated minimum is $1,000,000 for swingline borrowings; no other minimum borrowing or prepayment amounts are given.
rows.ts_quote: The Borrowers may prepay the Senior Credit Facility in whole or in part at any time without premium or penalty, subject to compensation for losses. The unutilized portion of the commitments under the Revolving Credit Facility may be irrevocably reduced or terminated
rows.ts_location: PDF p.6 (Optional Prepayments and Commitment Reductions); PDF p.2 (Swingline)
rows.ca_value: Voluntary prepayment of RC and Term Loans without premium or penalty, plus s.3.05 breakage. Notice is 3 Business Days for Term SOFR Loans and same day for Base Rate Loans. Prepayment minimums: Term SOFR $3M plus $1M multiples, Base Rate $1M plus $100k multiples, Swing Line $100k. RC and sublimit reductions need 5 Business Days' notice in $10M plus $1M multiples. Unused Term Commitments can be terminated. Notices may be conditional on other financing. Borrowing minimums: Term SOFR $3M plus $1M multiples, Base Rate $1M plus $500k multiples, Swing Line $1M.
rows.ca_quote: from time to time voluntarily prepay Revolving Credit Loans or Term Loans in whole or in part without premium or penalty
rows.explanation: The no-premium prepayment right with breakage and the RC reduction right match. The CA adds customary notice periods and minimum amounts that the TS did not specify, and also allows conditional notices, which favours the Borrowers.

rows.attribute: Interest periods, notice periods and day count
rows.ts_value: Term SOFR interest periods of 1, 3 or 6 months, subject to availability. Interest is paid at the end of each period, at least quarterly, and at maturity. Term SOFR is set two U.S. government securities business days before the period. LCs require four business days' notice, or five for certain currencies. Day count is actual/365-366 for Base Rate loans and actual/360 for everything else.
rows.ts_quote: The Borrowers may select interest periods of one, three or six months for Term SOFR loans, subject to availability.
rows.ts_location: PDF p.14 (Addendum I - Interest Rates); PDF p.2 (LC notice); PDF p.15 (Calculation of Interest and Fees)
rows.ca_value: Interest Periods of 1, 3 or 6 months, or any other period of 12 months or less with the consent of all Lenders and the Agent, subject to availability. Interest is paid at period end and every three months for longer periods; Base Rate interest is paid quarterly. Loan Notices are due by 9:00 a.m. two Business Days before Term SOFR borrowings and on the same day for Base Rate. LC Applications are due at least two Business Days before issuance. Day count is 365/366 for Base Rate Loans and a 360-day year otherwise. Loans made on the Closing Date must be Base Rate Loans unless a funding indemnity letter is delivered; no Term SOFR Loans during a Default without Required Lenders' consent; at most 5 Interest Periods for the Term Facility and 10 for the RC.
rows.ca_quote: ending on the date one, three or six months thereafter, as selected by the Company in its Loan Notice, or such other period that is twelve months or less requested by the Company and consented to by all of the Lenders and the Administrative Agent
rows.ca_location: s.1.01 'Interest Payment Date', 'Interest Period' (PDF p.14); s.2.01(a)-(b) (PDF pp.25-26); s.2.02(a), (c), (e) (PDF pp.26-27); s.2.03(b)(i) (PDF p.28); s.2.10(a) (PDF p.36)
rows.explanation: Interest period menu, payment frequency, SOFR fixing lag and day count all match. The CA shortens LC request notice from four or five business days to two Business Days and allows periods of up to 12 months with all-lender consent. These are minor operational differences in the Borrowers' favour. The CA also adds customary operational limits that the TS does not mention: Base Rate loans at closing unless a funding indemnity letter is delivered, no Term SOFR loans during a Default, and caps on the number of Interest Periods.

result.document_notes: TS: "Summary of Terms and Conditions" for Granite Construction Incorporated, "Up to $1,100,000,000 Senior Secured Credit Facility". It is attached to a Commitment Letter that was not provided. Doc ref 207388596_2, 16 PDF pages, no date shown. Pricing, fees and the pricing grid are in Addendum I (PDF pp.14-15). The pricing grid is garbled in the -layout text, and pdftoppm is not installed, so neither the analyst nor the reviewer could render the PDF page. The grid values come from a pdftotext -raw extraction of TS PDF page 15: L1 <1.50x 17.5/125.0/83.3/25.0; L2 1.50x 20.0/150.0/100.0/50.0; L3 2.00x 25.0/162.5/105.0/62.5; L4 2.50x 30.0/175.0/120.0/75.0; L5 3.25x 35.0/200.0/135.0/100.0. Reading each column of the -layout text from top to bottom gives the same values. CA: Fifth Amended and Restated Credit Agreement dated as of August 5, 2025 (Execution Version 207163075_10), 84 PDF pages. Bank of America, N.A. is Administrative Agent, Collateral Agent, Swing Line Lender and L/C Issuer. It amends and restates the Fourth A&R Credit Agreement dated June 2, 2022, as the TS anticipated. It is a full restated agreement, not an amendment with a conformed copy. The text includes the signature pages, Schedule 1.01(g) (Guarantors) and Schedule 2.01 (Commitments); exhibits are listed but not reproduced. The CA's printed page numbers differ from PDF page numbers; all references use the PDF page markers. Limitations: (1) the Fee Letter dated June 30, 2025 was not provided, so upfront, arrangement and fronting fee amounts cannot be reconciled; (2) the CA defines the Closing Date as the date the Section 4.01 conditions are satisfied and does not give it as a calendar date, so the five-year tenor is checked against the August 5, 2025 agreement date; (3) the TS is undated. Key findings: (a) commitments were upsized from up to $1.1bn (RC $550m + TL $550m) to $1.275bn (RC $600m + TL $675m); (b) the CA adds a delayed-draw term feature (up to $75m within 6 months, Term Loans to the Company only) with a new ticking fee; (c) the CA adds a 1.00% Base Rate floor; (d) the CA's 105% LC cash-collateral mechanic is stricter than the TS (cure to 100% of the sublimit, any cause), and the CA allows up to three additional L/C Issuers; (e) incremental terms differ in both directions: junior IED, fixed-basket reclassification, LCA carve-outs and a no-default test only at effectiveness favour the Borrowers, while a rep bring-down, pro forma covenant compliance and WAL tests favour the lenders; (f) the CA narrows the default-interest step-up (automatic only on overdue principal; otherwise Required Lenders' request plus written notice); (g) the CA adds Level 5 pricing for late Compliance Certificates and retroactive repricing. Every tier and column of the pricing grid matches, and all first-pass quotes were checked verbatim against the text files.

The CA weakens two TS unanimous rights: pro rata sharing changes need only a majority of the affected class instead of each Lender, and subordination needs only each directly affected Lender instead of each Lender. It also lets the Required Lenders waive default interest, a reduction of interest that the TS reserved to each affected Lender, and lets the Required Lenders add new ratably sharing facilities. These changes dilute minority lender protection and favour the Borrowers.

rows.ts_value: Assignments to financial institutions, minimum $5,000,000, with consents not unreasonably withheld. Borrower consent is required for assignees in a similar line of business, and for all others unless an EoD is continuing or the assignee is a Lender, affiliate or Approved Fund; consent is deemed after 5 business days, except for competitor assignments. Administrative Agent consent for non-Lender assignees; Fronting Bank and Swingline Lender consent for any assignment. $3,500 fee, waivable. Federal Reserve pledges permitted. Participant voting limited to significant matters. Assignments must be pro rata across facilities. Absolute bar: no assignments to competitors of the Company or its subsidiaries.
rows.ts_quote: Notwithstanding the foregoing, under no circumstances will any assignments be permitted to be made to competitors of the Company or any of its subsidiaries.
rows.ca_value: §10.06: assignments to Eligible Assignees, minimum $5,000,000 (revolver and term) unless the Administrative Agent and Company consent. Company consent (not unreasonably withheld) is needed for assignments to persons in similar lines of business or competitors, but only if the Company designated them by written notice at least 10 Business Days in advance; withholding is deemed reasonable and designation is not retroactive. Otherwise Company consent is needed unless an EoD is continuing or the assignee is a Lender, Affiliate or Approved Fund, and is deemed given after 5 Business Days. Administrative Agent consent for non-Lender assignees. L/C Issuer consent only for revolver assignments that increase L/C exposure; Swing Line Lender consent for revolver assignments. $3,500 fee, waivable. No assignments to Borrowers or their affiliates, Defaulting Lenders or natural persons. Assignments pro rata across revolver and term. Participant voting limited to the first proviso of §10.01. Federal Reserve pledges permitted.
rows.ca_quote: if such assignment is to a Person that is engaged in similar lines of business of, or is a competitor to, the Company or any of its Subsidiaries, which Person has been designated by the Company in its reasonable discretion by written notice to the Administrative Agent
rows.explanation: Mechanics match: minimums, fee, deemed consent, Administrative Agent consent, participations, Federal Reserve pledges and pro rata assignment. But the TS absolute bar on assignments to competitors becomes a Company consent right that applies only to competitors designated in advance on 10 Business Days' notice. Undesignated competitors can take assignments under the ordinary consent rules, and without Company consent during an EoD. Fronting bank and swingline consent is also narrowed to revolver assignments. This favours the lenders' ability to transfer.

result.document_notes: TS: 'Summary of Terms and Conditions' for Granite Construction Incorporated, 'Up to $1,100,000,000 Senior Secured Credit Facility' (doc ref 207388596_2). It is a formal term sheet annexed to a commitment letter, is undated and runs 16 PDF pages, with Addendum I on pricing, fees and expenses. Many terms (reps, covenants, EoDs, yield protection, collateral) are set as 'substantially similar/identical to the Existing Credit Agreement'. CA: Fifth Amended and Restated Credit Agreement dated as of August 5, 2025 (Execution Version 207163075_10), 84 PDF pages. It is a full amendment and restatement of the Fourth A&R Credit Agreement dated June 2, 2022, not a short-form amendment, so it was reconciled as a standalone agreement. Limitations: (1) The Existing Credit Agreement and Existing Security Agreement were not provided, so TS terms defined by reference to them (EoDs, basket sizes, collateral 'Excluded Property', reps 'substantially similar') cannot be fully verified. (2) The CA text has only Schedules 1.01(g) (Guarantors) and 2.01 (Commitments). The exhibits (Guaranty, Pledge Agreement, Security Agreement) and other schedules (e.g. 5.06, 6.16, 7.01(x)) are not included, so items such as 'guarantees of payment not collection' cannot be checked. (3) The CA text extraction runs paragraphs together, and inline page numbers in the text differ from the PDF page markers; all CA page references use the [PDF PAGE n] markers. (4) The CA table of contents lists §5.20 'Taxpayer Identification Number' but the body shows '5.20 [Reserved]'. (5) Facility amounts, pricing, fees, accordion sizing and other group A items are excluded. The CA facility amounts ($600M revolver / $675M term with a delayed draw) differ from the TS ($550M / $550M) and are left to group A. All quotes were machine-checked against the text files with whitespace collapsed. Reviewer notes: §9.10 (Collateral and Guaranty Matters, including the Collateral Agent appointment) sits on PDF p.69, and the B03/B06 references were corrected. B08 was reclassified to 'differs' because §7.03(p) limits the acquisition-debt basket to assumed debt. Three TS mechanics outside group A were added: L/C currencies and notice (X20), swingline mechanics (X21) and day count (X22). The L/C 105% FX cash collateral and the rate replacement / SOFR Adjustment points are group A (prepayments / benchmarks) and were not added.

Term SOFR = forward-looking term rate for the interest period based on SOFR administered by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York (no term-rate administrator such as CME is named), floor zero; USD only. EURIBOR (Alternative Currency Term Rate) is from the Bloomberg screen two TARGET Days before the period, floor zero. The CA adds a zero floor on the Federal Funds Rate, and removes the Term SOFR leg from the Base Rate when it is used as the fallback under s.2.19. No credit spread adjustment.

result.document_notes: TS: "Honeywell International Inc. Summary of Terms and Conditions - $3,000,000,000 364-Day Multi-Currency Revolving Credit Facility". It is an indicative, undated 10-page term sheet (footer "2026 Honeywell Term Sheet"), and page 10 is the 364-Day Pricing Grid. The TS says documentation will be "substantially similar" to the Existing 364-Day Credit Agreement dated March 17, 2025. In the layout extraction of TS pages 2-9 the left-column headings are out of line with the body text (for example "Commitment Fee:" and "Interest Rates and" sit inside the Commitment Reduction paragraph). Each paragraph was mapped to its heading by order, and quotes were taken only from clean text runs. CA: a new, stand-alone agreement, not an amendment. It is the 364-DAY CREDIT AGREEMENT dated as of March 6, 2026 (Exhibit 10.1, Execution Version) among Honeywell International Inc. as Company, the Initial Lenders, and Bank of America, N.A. as Administrative Agent, with Goldman Sachs Bank USA, Morgan Stanley Senior Funding and MUFG as Syndication Agents (the TS names only GS and MS; a party point for another group). The file has 113 PDF pages, ending with the signature pages (PDF p.81-113). The table of contents section numbering in the text extraction is misaligned (for example it shows s.2.13 as [Reserved]); section references here follow the body text. Limitations: (1) Schedule I (Commitments), Schedule 9.02 and Exhibits A-D appear in the table of contents but are NOT in the CA file. Per-lender and total commitments could therefore not be tied to Schedule I; the $3,000,000,000 total is taken from the cover page. (2) The CA Applicable Margin grid (PDF page 9) is garbled in the layout text, but level-by-level values were re-confirmed in review against the layout fragments and the TS grid: margins 0.50/0.625/0.75/0.875/1.00/1.125% and commitment fees 0.020/0.030/0.040/0.050/0.075/0.090%, with identical rating thresholds (AA-/Aa3, A+/A1, A/A2, A-/A3, BBB+/Baa1, below). (3) The CA does not record the actual Effective Date. The March 5, 2027 Termination Date matches the TS formula (364 days after closing) only if the Effective Date was March 6, 2026. (4) An extra row, X01 (Change of Control lender termination right), was added because it appears under the TS "Commitment Reduction" heading and the CA adds mechanics to it. Main findings: the economics (amount, currencies, margin and fee grids, term-out fee, day counts, minimum amounts, 103% currency test, Spin-Off step-down to $2bn) reconcile. The differences: the CA term-out requires a full rep bring-down, including MAC, litigation, ERISA and environmental reps that the TS limits to the Closing Date, plus 15 days' notice and conversion of all Advances (material, lender-favourable); a split-rating rule and no-rating default to Level 6; default interest extended to overdue interest and fees; a shorter Term SOFR borrowing notice (2 Business Days against 3 in the TS); an added non-ratable commitment reduction right (s.2.06(c)), with the Rating Condition attached to it rather than to lender replacement as in the TS; small borrower-favourable mechanics on the $3,500 replacement/assignment fee (assignee may pay; Agent may waive); and a 60-day borrowing suspension after a Change of Control. Review corrections: A05 rep scope and page reference, A10 TS Term SOFR description (CME is named only in the CA), A15 status changed from match to match_minor_drafting, and clarifying explanations on A13, A18, A19 and X01. All quotes were checked verbatim against the text files.

result.document_notes:
TS: a 10-page "Summary of Terms and Conditions" (indicative term sheet) for Honeywell International Inc.'s $3,000,000,000 364-Day Multi-Currency Revolving Credit Facility. It is undated; the footer reads "2026 Honeywell Term Sheet" and the 364-Day Pricing Grid is on PDF page 10. On TS PDF pages 2-9 the two-column layout came out garbled: the left-hand captions do not line up with their text, so section headings were inferred from caption order. For example, the Change of Control and Spin Off text sits under "Commitment Reduction" on page 2. Every TS quote was checked mechanically against the text file (whitespace collapsed) and avoids lines with misplaced captions.

CA: an executed new standalone agreement, not an amendment: the 364-DAY CREDIT AGREEMENT dated as of March 6, 2026 (Execution Version, filed as Exhibit 10.1). The parties are Honeywell International Inc. (Company), 32 Initial Lenders and Bank of America, N.A. as Administrative Agent. It refinances and terminates the 364-Day Credit Agreement dated March 17, 2025 (s.3.01(g)). The CA table of contents (PDF pages 3-5) is garbled in extraction (section numbers do not line up with titles); section references here are taken from the body headings, e.g. s.9.06 is Assignments and Participations and s.9.10 is Governing Law.

Limitations:
(1) The CA text (113 PDF pages) ends at the signature pages. Schedule I (Commitments), Schedule 9.02 and Exhibits A-D (form of Note, Notice of Borrowing, Assignment and Assumption, General Counsel opinion) are listed in the table of contents but not included, so individual lender commitments and the form of opinion could not be reconciled.
(2) The TS ties most legal terms (reps, covenants, events of default, defaulting lenders, taxes, Eligible Assignee, Rating Condition) to the Existing 364-Day Agreement dated March 17, 2025, using "similar to" or "no less favorable to the Company than". That agreement was not provided, so the CA could only be checked against what the TS itself says. Borrower-favourable differences flagged here, including the B12 judgment-default aggregation point, may simply carry over from the existing agreement.
(3) Benchmark replacement (X11), the Spin-Off commitment reduction (X03), and the added rows for currencies (X17), borrowing notice mechanics (X18) and interest payment dates/day count (X19) may overlap with Group A. They are included for completeness. X18 records a real difference: Term SOFR borrowing notice is 2 Business Days in the CA against 3 business days in the TS.
(4) Cross-group point for the Group A term-out reviewer (B11): CA s.2.07/3.03 makes the Term Loan Election subject to a full bring-down of the reps, including no MAC since Dec 31, 2024, whereas the TS conditions it only on no default or event of default. CA s.2.07 also needs at least 15 days' notice of the election.
(5) Review results: all 62 original quotes were confirmed verbatim. Status changes: B04 (to differs), X08 (to match_minor_drafting). Materiality change: B12 (to material: the judgment EoD no longer aggregates). Direction changes: B13 and X16 (to neutral). Wording or substance corrections: B03, B09 and B15.

rows.ca_value: Section 2.19: request at least 30 and not more than 60 days before any anniversary of the Effective Date for a one-year extension. Lenders respond at least 15 days before, and silence is deemed non-consent. The Agent notifies the Company not later than 10 days before. The extension is effective if Lenders holding AT LEAST 50% of the Revolving Credit Commitments consent, subject to the Section 3.03 conditions. Because the 3.03(a)(i) carve-out of the no-MAC (4.01(e) last sentence), litigation (4.01(f)) and other reps applies only to Borrowings and issuances, all representations, including no MAC and no litigation, must be true on each Extension Date, and no Default may exist. Non-Consenting Lenders terminate at the unextended date. Assuming Lenders must take at least $25,000,000. There is no term-out option.

The consent threshold falls from 'more than 50%' in the TS to 'at least 50%' in the CA, which favours the borrower only at exactly 50%. Against that, the CA adds lender-favourable terms the TS does not state: deemed non-consent for silent Lenders, a $25M minimum for Assuming Lenders, and a full Section 3.03 bring-down on each Extension Date that includes the no-MAC and litigation reps. The net effect is mixed.

The Company may offer the increase to (x) existing lenders, who have no obligation to participate, or (y) third-party institutions. The Increase Date must be at least 90 days before the earliest scheduled Termination Date. Caps are $4,500,000,000 before the Spin-Off Date and $3,500,000,000 on and after it. Section 3.03 conditions must be met on the request date and the Increase Date: all reps true in all material respects (including no MAC and litigation, because the 3.03(a)(i) carve-out applies only to Borrowings and issuances) and no Default. The request goes first to existing Lenders (2.18(b)). The Company may approach Eligible Assignees only for any shortfall (2.18(c)). Allocation among over-subscribing Lenders is agreed between the Company and the Agent, and each increased commitment needs Issuing Bank and Swing Line Bank approval, not to be unreasonably withheld. Eligible Assignees must be approved by each Issuing Bank and Swing Line Bank and commit $25,000,000 or an integral multiple. Board resolutions and an opinion are required.

rows.ts_location: PDF p.3, 'Commitment Fee'; PDF p.12, grid
rows.ca_value: Applicable Percentage: Level 1 0.040%, Level 2 0.050%, Level 3 0.065%, Level 4 0.080%, Level 5 0.10%, Level 6 0.110%. It is charged on the Unused Commitment (Fee Calculation), meaning the commitment less revolving advances and the ratable L/C share. Swing line usage is NOT deducted. It is payable quarterly in arrears on the last day of March, June, September and December, starting June 30, 2026, and on the Termination Date. Defaulting Lenders earn no fee. Day count is 365/366.
rows.ca_quote: a commitment fee on the aggregate amount of such Lender's Unused Commitment (Fee Calculation) from the date hereof
rows.ca_location: Section 2.05(a) PDF p.40; Section 1.01 'Applicable Percentage' PDF p.10; 'Unused Commitment (Fee Calculation)' PDF p.30; Section 2.13(b) PDF p.53
rows.explanation: All six fee tiers, the payment dates and the day count match. The CA fee base excludes swing line advances from usage, so the fee accrues on swing-line-drawn amounts. This is market-standard but slightly favours lenders compared with a plain 'unused commitment'.

rows.attribute: Letter of credit participation fee and fronting fee
rows.ts_value: L/C fee is a rate per annum equal to the Applicable Margin for Term SOFR Advances. No fronting fee is stated.
rows.ts_quote: A rate per annum equal to the Applicable Margin for Term SOFR Advances.
rows.ca_value: The Applicable Letter of Credit Rate equals the Applicable Margin for Term SOFR Advances. It is charged on each Lender's ratable share of L/C Available Amounts and is payable quarterly in arrears on the third Business Day after each quarter-end, starting with the quarter ending June 30, 2026. It steps up by 1% during a payment Event of Default when default interest applies. Issuing Bank (fronting) fees are as separately agreed between the Company and each Issuing Bank (Section 2.05(b)(ii)).
rows.ca_quote: "Applicable Letter of Credit Rate" means, as of any date, a percentage per annum equal to the Applicable Margin for Term SOFR Advances.
rows.ca_location: Section 1.01 'Applicable Letter of Credit Rate' PDF p.9; Section 2.05(b)(i)-(ii) PDF pp.40-41
rows.explanation: The L/C participation fee is identical, and the +1% default step-up is consistent with the TS's 100 bp default margin increase. The TS gives no fronting fee, and the CA leaves it to separate agreement, so no inconsistency arises.

rows.attribute: Upfront, ticking, term-out, extension or other fees stated in the TS
rows.ts_value: No upfront, ticking, term-out, extension or utilization fees are stated. The only other fee is a $3,500 Agent administrative fee per assignment, paid by the parties other than the Company, plus a $3,500 fee the Company pays when a replacement Lender is not an existing Lender. Expense reimbursement also applies.
rows.ts_quote: The parties to the assignment (other than the Company) shall pay to the Agent an administrative fee of $3,500 per assignment.
rows.ts_location: PDF pp.9-10, 'Assignments and Participations' and 'Yield Protection, Taxes, and Other Deductions' (lender replacement); PDF p.11, 'Expenses'
rows.ca_value: No upfront, ticking, term-out, extension or utilization fees appear. Section 9.06(b)(iv) sets a $3,500 processing and recordation fee per assignment, delivered by the parties to the assignment, which the Agent may waive at its sole discretion. On a Company-driven replacement, 'such assignee or the Company' pays it if the assignee is not an existing Lender (Section 2.06(b)(iv)). Agent's fees are as separately agreed (Section 2.05(c)).
rows.ca_quote: together with a processing and recordation fee of $3,500
rows.ca_location: Section 9.06(b)(iv) PDF p.98; Section 2.06(b)(iv) PDF p.41; Section 2.05(c) PDF p.41
rows.explanation: The $3,500 amounts match, and neither document contains upfront, ticking, term-out or extension fees. The mechanics differ slightly. The CA lets the Agent waive the assignment fee. On a replacement, the CA lets either the assignee or the Company pay the fee, whereas the TS puts it on the Company. Any arrangement or upfront fees would sit in fee letters, which were not provided.

rows.ts_value: During a payment event of default, the margin on unpaid principal of each Advance increases by 100 bps p.a. Non-Base Rate Advances convert to Base Rate Advances at the end of the current interest period, with non-USD Advances exchanged into USD.
rows.ts_quote: Upon the occurrence and during the continuance of any payment event of default, the Applicable Margin on the unpaid principal amount of each Advance will increase by 100 basis points per annum
rows.ca_value: During an Event of Default under Section 6.01(a) (payment default), unpaid principal of Revolving Credit Advances bears interest at 1% p.a. above the applicable rate. Swing Line Advances are not covered, except overdue swing lines during the Section 2.07(c) refinancing window. Overdue interest, fees and other amounts also bear interest at 1% above the rate. The L/C fee rises by 1%. Term Rate Advances convert or are exchanged into USD Base Rate Advances at the end of the Interest Period, and SONIA advances on the next Interest Payment Date. New Term Rate and SONIA borrowings are suspended (Section 2.09(d)).
rows.ca_quote: Upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an Event of Default under Section 6.01(a), each Borrower shall pay interest on (i) the unpaid principal amount of each Revolving Credit Advance
rows.ca_location: Section 2.08(b) PDF p.47; Section 2.09(d) PDF p.48; Section 2.05(b)(i) PDF p.41; Section 2.07(c) PDF p.45; Section 6.01(a) PDF p.78
rows.explanation: The payment-default trigger, the +100 bp step-up on principal and the conversion to USD Base Rate at the end of the Interest Period match. The CA also charges default interest on overdue interest and fees and suspends new Term Rate and SONIA borrowings, both of which modestly favour lenders. The CA's step-up applies to Revolving Credit Advances rather than 'each Advance', so swing line advances are largely outside it. This is a small offset in the borrower's favour, because unpaid swing lines are refinanced into revolving advances.

rows.ts_value: No amortization: borrow, repay and reborrow, with all Advances repaid by the Termination Date. Mandatory prepayment applies if the USD equivalent of all Advances exceeds 103% of the Facility Amount, bringing it down to 100%. Excess outstandings over the reduced commitments must be repaid on the Spin Off.
rows.ts_quote: If at any time the dollar equivalent value of all Advances exceeds 103% of the Facility Amount, the Borrowers shall promptly make a mandatory prepayment to reduce the dollar equivalent value of all Advances to 100% of the Facility Amount.
rows.ts_location: PDF p.5, 'Repayment' and 'Dollar Equivalent Value Limitation for All Advances'; PDF p.2 (Spin Off repayment)
rows.ca_value: Bullet repayment of revolving advances on the Termination Date (Section 2.07(a)). Swing line advances are repaid on the Swing Line Maturity Date. Mandatory prepayment applies if USD advances plus the USD equivalent of Alternative Currency advances plus L/C Available Amounts exceed 103% of aggregate Commitments, reducing them to 100% by prepayment or by a Cash Deposit Account deposit, with FX measured 3 Business Days prior. Section 2.06(f)(iii) requires repayment of any excess on the Spin-Off Date.
rows.ca_quote: exceeds 103% of the aggregate Commitments of the Lenders on such date, the Company and each other Borrower, if any, shall thereupon promptly prepay
rows.ca_location: Section 2.07(a) PDF p.44; Section 2.10(b) PDF p.49; Section 2.06(f) PDF pp.43-44
rows.explanation: The no-amortization bullet structure and the 103%/100% currency-fluctuation test match. The CA includes L/C exposure in the test, which favours lenders, and allows cash collateral instead of prepayment, which favours the borrower, so the net effect is neutral.

rows.attribute: Optional prepayments, commitment reductions, minimum borrowing amounts
rows.ts_value: Commitment reductions on at least 3 business days' notice, in a minimum of $10,000,000 plus $1,000,000 multiples, with no reinstatement. Prepayment without penalty on notice by 11:00 a.m. same day for Base Rate, or 11:00 a.m. two business days prior for Term SOFR, EURIBOR, SONIA, TIBOR and Term CORRA, in a minimum of $10,000,000 plus $1,000,000 increments, with breakage for the borrower's account. Minimum borrowing is $10,000,000 plus $1,000,000 multiples. 'Other' item (4) lets the Company replace any Lender by assignment or by adding a new Lender, provided no Rating Condition is continuing and no more than 3 non-defaulting Lenders are replaced in a calendar year.
rows.ts_quote: The Company will have the right, upon at least three business days' notice, to terminate or cancel, in whole or in part, the unused portion of the commitments
rows.ts_location: PDF p.2, 'Commitment Reduction'; PDF p.4, 'Borrowings'; PDF p.5, 'Optional Prepayment'; PDF p.9, 'Other' item (4)
rows.ca_value: Section 2.06(a): ratable termination or reduction on at least 3 Business Days' notice, at least $10,000,000 or a $1,000,000 multiple above that, with no reinstatement. Section 2.10(a): prepayment by 11:00 a.m. two Business Days prior for Term Rate and SONIA advances and by 11:00 a.m. same day for Base Rate advances. Partial prepayments are at least $10,000,000 plus $1,000,000 multiples, with breakage under Section 9.04(c). Swing line minimum is 1,000,000 / $1,000,000. Section 2.01(a): minimum borrowing of $10,000,000 plus $1,000,000 multiples. Section 2.06(b): replacement by assignment on 10 Business Days' notice if no Event of Default, with at most three Non-Defaulting Lenders replaced per calendar year. Section 2.06(c): the Company may terminate an individual Lender's commitments outright, without replacement, at any time other than during a Rating Condition, capped each calendar year at the greater of three Lenders' commitments or $240,000,000.
rows.ca_quote: upon at least three Business Days' notice to the Administrative Agent, to terminate in whole or permanently reduce ratably in part the Unused Commitments of the Lenders, provided that each partial reduction shall be in an aggregate amount not less than $10,000,000
rows.ca_location: Section 2.06(a)-(c) PDF pp.41-42; Section 2.10(a) PDF pp.48-49; Section 2.01(a) PDF p.33
rows.explanation: Notice periods, minimums and multiples for reductions, prepayments and borrowings all match. The TS addresses lender replacement only, in 'Other' item (4), which requires no Rating Condition and allows at most 3 non-defaulting Lenders a year. The CA goes further. Section 2.06(c) lets the Company terminate a Lender's commitments without replacing it, up to the greater of three Lenders' commitments or $240M a year. Section 2.06(b) replacement is conditioned on no Event of Default rather than on no Rating Condition. Both favour the borrower.

rows.ts_location: PDF pp.3-4, 'Interest Rates and Interest Periods'; PDF p.4, 'Interest Payments' and 'Borrowings'; PDF p.5 (continuation)

rows.attribute: Change of Control lender commitment termination right (extra TS term)
rows.ts_value: If a Change of Control occurs, each Lender may, on at least 10 days' notice, terminate its commitment on the date 60 days after the Change of Control. Change of Control means acquisition of 50% or more of Voting Stock, or a change in the board majority within any 12-month period, with exceptions for board-approved replacements. No borrowing suspension is stated.
rows.ts_quote: If a Change of Control occurs each Lender may upon at least 10 days notice terminate its commitment on the date that is 60 days after such Change of Control.
rows.ts_location: PDF pp.2-3, 'Commitment Reduction' (Change of Control paragraphs)
rows.ca_value: Section 2.06(d): a Lender may give notice no later than 50 calendar days after a Change of Control, which preserves at least 10 days before the 60-day point. Termination of its Revolving Credit, Unissued L/C and Swing Line Commitments takes effect at the later of 60 days after the Change of Control and the end of the Interest Period of any outstanding Term Rate Advance. The notice does not accelerate outstanding advances. For 60 days after a Change of Control, borrowings and L/C issuance are suspended except for Base Rate advances, SONIA advances and Term Rate Advances with Interest Periods ending within 90 days. The CA's Change of Control definition matches the TS, except that the board test is measured over 'any period of twelve consecutive calendar months commencing at the Effective Date'.
rows.ca_quote: each Borrower's right to make a Borrowing or request the issuance of a Letter of Credit under this Agreement shall be suspended for a period of 60 calendar days
rows.ca_location: Section 2.06(d) PDF p.43; Section 1.01 'Change of Control' PDF p.13

The CA adds a 60-day suspension of new borrowings and L/C issuance after a Change of Control, which the TS does not state. Base Rate and short-dated borrowings remain available, which limits its effect. The deferral of termination to the end of the Interest Period slightly favours the borrower. The board-change limb, measured over twelve months 'commencing at the Effective Date', could be read as covering only the first year rather than the TS's 'any 12 month period'. That ambiguity favours the borrower.

result.document_notes:
TS: 12-page indicative 'Summary of Terms and Conditions' for Honeywell International Inc.'s $4,000,000,000 5-Year Multi-Currency Revolving Credit Facility. It is undated, carries the footer '2026 Honeywell Term Sheet' and attaches a 5-Year Pricing Grid on p.12. It is a formal term sheet, not a lender presentation. It says the 364-Day and 5-Year facilities may be documented together or separately, and only the 5-Year terms were reconciled. The -layout extraction misplaces the TS margin headings (e.g. 'Commitment Fee:' sits beside the Change of Control text on p.3), but the clause text is intact.

CA: new standalone FIVE YEAR CREDIT AGREEMENT dated as of March 6, 2026 (Exhibit 10.2, Execution Version), U.S. $4,000,000,000. The parties are Honeywell International Inc. as Company/Borrower, the Initial Lenders and Initial Swing Line Banks, and Bank of America, N.A. as Administrative Agent and Swing Line Agent. Bank of America is the only signatory designated as an Initial Swing Line Bank (signature pages PDF pp.110-111). The CA is not an amendment. Section 3.01(g) requires the Amended and Restated Five Year Credit Agreement dated March 18, 2024 to be repaid and terminated.

Limitations:
(1) The CA PDF has 142 pages and ends with the signature pages. Schedule I (Commitments, including Swing Line Commitments), Schedule 2.01(b), Schedule 9.02 and Exhibits A-F are not included. The per-lender commitments and the $500,000,000 swing line sublimit therefore cannot be verified, and the $4bn total rests on the cover page only. The Swing Line Commitment definition's proviso ('no less than its respective Revolving Credit Commitment') means the swing line cap is at least Bank of America's undisclosed revolving commitment.
(2) The CA table of contents for Article II is misaligned with the body (for example, it lists 'SECTION 2.18' as Prepayments), so section references follow the body text.
(3) The CA Applicable Margin grid on p.10 is misaligned in the layout text, but its six values run in tier order. The CA commitment fee grid and the TS p.12 grid read cleanly. All six margin tiers and all six commitment fee tiers match.
(4) The Effective Date is conditional under Section 3.01. The maturity reconciliation assumes the CA became effective on its stated date of March 6, 2026.
(5) Fee letters, including any upfront or arrangement fees, were not provided.

Page references use the [PDF PAGE n] markers. X01 (Change of Control lender termination right) was added because the TS states it under the commitment provisions. The TS lender-replacement right ('Other' item (4)) is reconciled in A18. All ts_quote and ca_quote strings were checked mechanically against the text files with whitespace collapsed, and all were found.
