rows.attribute: Events of default and thresholds (cross-default, judgment, grace periods)
rows.ts_value: No less favorable to the Company than the Existing 5-Year Agreement: (1) principal when due; interest or Commitment Fee within 3 business days; other amounts within 30 days. (2) Reps materially incorrect when made. (3) Covenant breach, with notice and cure periods as applicable. (4) Cross-default to payment defaults on principal Debt aggregating $500m, or to defaults permitting acceleration. Excludes Debt owed to institutions holding sufficient deposits, and Debt of China/India/CIS/Turkey subsidiaries (unsupported, government-caused, assets not over $500m individually or $650m collectively). (5) Unsatisfied judgment over $500m 'individually or in the aggregate', with the same carve-out. (6) Bankruptcy/insolvency. (7) ERISA events with liability over $500m.
rows.ts_quote: (5) Unsatisfied judgment or order in excess of $500,000,000 individually or in the aggregate.
rows.ca_value: 6.01(a): Revolving principal when due; Swing Line principal, interest, commitment fees and LC commissions within 3 Business Days; other amounts within 30 days unless contested in good faith and placed in Escrow. (b) Reps incorrect in any material respect. (c) Company repudiates the guarantee. (d) Breach of 5.01(h)(v) with no grace; breach of 5.02(a) uncured 30 days after notice; other covenants uncured 30 days after notice or officer knowledge. (e) Cross-payment default or acceleration of Debt of at least $500m in aggregate of the Company or a Material Subsidiary, with the deposit carve-out, a carve-out for Spin-Off and refinancing prepayments, and the Exempt Countries carve-out ($500m / $650m book value). (f) Bankruptcy of the Company or a Material Subsidiary (30 days for involuntary cases), with the Exempt Countries carve-out. (g) A money judgment over $500m against the Company or a Material Subsidiary, with enforcement begun and 10 consecutive days unstayed, with the Exempt Countries carve-out. (h) A non-monetary MAE judgment unstayed for 60 days. (i) Licences revoked. (j) ERISA: over $500m, withdrawal liability over 6% of Net Tangible Assets, or multiemployer contribution increase over $500m. Acceleration by Majority Lenders; automatic on US bankruptcy.
rows.ca_quote: (g) Any judgment or order for the payment of money in excess of $500,000,000 shall be rendered against the Company or any of its Material Subsidiaries
rows.ca_location: Section 6.01(a)-(j), PDF pp.78-81
rows.explanation: The $500m thresholds, the Exempt Countries carve-out ($500m / $650m) and the payment grace periods match. The CA is looser than the TS wording in several ways: (1) judgments are tested per judgment, not 'individually or in the aggregate', and also require enforcement proceedings plus a 10-consecutive-day unstayed period; (2) cross-default, bankruptcy and judgment tests apply only to the Company and Material Subsidiaries (10% revenue/asset test, plus each Designated Subsidiary); (3) swing line principal gets a 3-Business-Day grace period; (4) contested amounts placed in Escrow are excluded; (5) cross-default excludes intra-group Debt and payments barred by law, carves out Spin-Off and refinancing prepayments, and counts guaranteed or secured third-party Debt only when the Company or Subsidiary itself fails to pay; (6) the Exempt Countries carve-out is extended to the bankruptcy event, where the TS applied it only to cross-default and judgments. In the Lenders' favour, the CA limits the Exempt Countries carve-out to Subsidiaries (TS: 'subsidiary or affiliate'), adds a cross-default limb for required prepayment, redemption or repurchase offers, and adds guarantee repudiation, non-monetary judgment, licence revocation and two further ERISA triggers (withdrawal liability over 6% of Net Tangible Assets; multiemployer contribution increase over $500m). On balance the changes favour the Borrower.

rows.ts_value: Change of Control means: (i) any person (other than the Company, its subsidiaries or employee benefit plans) holding under 50% of the Company's Voting Stock acquires 50% or more; or (ii) in any 12-month period, the majority of the board changes, unless the replacements were elected or nominated by a majority of the remaining directors. Consequence: each Lender may, on at least 10 days' notice, terminate its commitment on the date 60 days after the Change of Control. Covenant: notice of change of control.

rows.ca_value: Definition: (i) any Person or 'group' (within the meaning of Exchange Act s.13/14) beneficially owning under 50% acquires 50% or more of voting power; (ii) during any 12 consecutive months 'commencing at the Effective Date', the board majority changes, with the same approved-replacement exception. Section 2.06(d): each Lender may give notice no later than 50 calendar days after the Change of Control. Termination takes effect on the later of 60 calendar days after the Change of Control or the end of any outstanding Term Rate Advance's Interest Period. On a Change of Control, Borrowings and LC requests are suspended for 60 days, except Base Rate, Alternative Currency Daily Rate and Term Rate Advances with Interest Periods ending within 90 days. Termination does not accelerate Advances. Section 5.01(k): notice to the Agent within 10 calendar days.
rows.ca_quote: In the event that a Change of Control occurs, each Lender may, by notice to the Company and the Administrative Agent given not later than 50 calendar days after such Change of Control, terminate its Revolving Credit Commitment,
rows.ca_location: Section 1.01 'Change of Control' p.13; Section 2.06(d) p.43; Section 5.01(k) p.76
rows.explanation: The 50%/board trigger and the 60-day lender put match. The 50-day notice deadline equals the TS's 'at least 10 days' notice' before day 60. The CA adds two mechanics the TS does not mention: a 60-day suspension of new Borrowings and LC issuance (except Base Rate and short-dated advances), which favours the Lenders, and a termination date that can slip to the end of an outstanding Interest Period, which favours the Borrower. The CA also adds 'group' to limb (i). Limb (ii) of the CA tests 'any period of twelve consecutive calendar months commencing at the Effective Date'. That wording could be read as confining the board-change test to the first 12 months from the Effective Date, whereas the TS tests any 12-month period. Read that way, it narrows the trigger in the Borrower's favour.

rows.ca_value: 2.11(a)/(b): increased costs and capital/liquidity, including Dodd-Frank and Basel III regardless of date, with a 90-day lookback (2.11(d)) and a general-practice condition (2.11(e)). 2.14: tax gross-up with the same exclusions (lender income and franchise taxes, US net income taxes, FATCA). 2.11(c) and 2.14(g): the Company may force assignment by a Lender claiming increased costs or taxes if no Default exists. 2.06(b): the Company may force assignment by any Lender, including a Defaulting Lender, on 10 Business Days' notice if no Event of Default exists, up to three Non-Defaulting Lenders per calendar year, with a $3,500 fee for new assignees. 2.06(c): non-ratable termination of a Lender's commitments, allowed except during a Rating Condition (both S&P and Moody's below BBB-/Baa3) and capped at the greater of 3 Lenders or $240m per year. 2.20: Defaulting Lender reallocation and cash collateral. 9.09: mitigation.

rows.explanation: Yield protection, the tax exclusions, the 3-per-year replacement cap and the $3,500 fee match. The replacement conditions are drafted differently from the TS. Replacing a Lender for yield protection or taxes is blocked by any Default (TS: only an EoD or unmatured payment/bankruptcy default), which favours the Lenders. Replacing a Defaulting Lender under 2.06(b) is blocked only by an Event of Default, not by an unmatured payment or bankruptcy default as in the TS, which favours the Borrower. The general replacement right in 2.06(b) has no Rating Condition test, which favours the Borrower; the Rating Condition limit applies instead to non-ratable termination under 2.06(c). It does add a no-Event-of-Default condition that TS item (4) does not state, which favours the Lenders. The 90-day lookback and general-practice limits also favour the Borrower.

result.document_notes: TS: "Honeywell International Inc. Summary of Terms and Conditions - $4,000,000,000 5-Year Multi-Currency Revolving Credit Facility" (footer "2026 Honeywell Term Sheet"). It is undated, marked indicative only, and has 11 pages of terms plus a 5-Year Pricing Grid on PDF p.12. It is addressed to prospective lenders. The TS uses a two-column layout. In the pdftotext extraction the left-hand headings often sit beside unrelated text (for example "Commitment Fee:" appears next to the Change of Control text on p.3, "Loan Documentation:" next to the Availability text on p.5, and "Covenants:" next to the reps list on p.7), so terms were mapped by their content, not by the adjacent heading. Many TS terms are stated only as "similar to (and no less favorable to the Company than) the Existing 5-Year Agreement" (the Amended and Restated Five Year Credit Agreement dated March 18, 2024). The TS also mentions a 364-Day Facility that this CA does not cover. CA: a new standalone "FIVE YEAR CREDIT AGREEMENT" dated as of March 6, 2026 (SEC Exhibit 10.2, Execution Version). Parties: Honeywell International Inc. as Borrower, and Bank of America, N.A. as Administrative Agent and Swing Line Agent. Amount: U.S. $4,000,000,000. It is not an amendment. Instead it requires repayment and termination of the March 18, 2024 agreement as a closing condition (Section 3.01(g)). Article VIII numbering in the CA is irregular: there are two Sections 8.07 (Resignation of Agent at p.88 and Non-Reliance at p.90), followed by 8.08 Other Agents, 8.09 Lender ERISA and 8.10 Erroneous Payments (pp.90-91). Limitations: (1) The CA PDF (142 pages) ends at the signature pages. Schedule I (Commitments), Schedule 2.01(b), Schedule 9.02 and Exhibits A-F (forms of Note, Designation Letter, opinions and so on) are listed in the table of contents but are not in the file. Per-lender commitments, swing line and LC commitment allocations, and the agreed forms therefore could not be reconciled. (2) The Existing 5-Year Agreement was not provided. Where the TS defers to it (basket levels, grace periods, Rating Condition, Eligible Assignee, Defaulting Lender provisions), the CA could only be checked against the TS's express wording, and "substantially similar / no less favorable" could not be verified. (3) Group A economic terms (amount, maturity, accordion, extension, sublimits, benchmarks, pricing grid, fees, prepayments, interest mechanics, benchmark replacement) are excluded here under the instructions. Borrowing notice and minimums were not clearly in either group and are covered in added row X17, where the Term SOFR notice period differs (TS 3 business days, CA 2 Business Days). (4) The TS has no financial covenant, sustainability/ESG pricing, ratings condition precedent or cashless-rollover terms, and the CA has no leverage, coverage, net worth or EBITDA test, so no rows were raised for those. All ts_quote and ca_quote fields were checked mechanically against the text files (whitespace collapsed) and appear verbatim.

Other terms of incremental term loans may in no event be more restrictive, taken as a whole, than the existing Facilities Documentation. No Lender is obliged to participate. For Limited Condition Transactions, the default and covenant conditions are tested on the LCT Test Date at the Company's election. No minimum amount is stated.

Ratio capacity is used first unless the Company elects otherwise, with automatic reclassification. Permitted Earlier Maturity Debt is the greater of $83.0m and 25% of EBITDA. Differences from the TS: (1) minimum request of $25,000,000; (2) incremental term loans may not mature before the Latest Maturity Date (latest of all facilities); (3) LCT relief on the no-Default and pro forma covenant conditions applies only 'to the extent agreed by the lenders providing such Incremental Facility'; (4) ratio and pro forma covenant tests without netting the incremental proceeds; (5) no express elective later reclassification (only automatic); (6) borrower-favourable: other terms of an Incremental Term Loan need only 'reflect market terms' OR be no more restrictive than existing terms, as determined by the Company in good faith (Section 2.16(a)(vi)).

rows.ca_location: Section 1.01 'Incremental Available Amount' p.72, 'Incremental Fixed Amount' and 'Incremental Ratio Amount' pp.73-74, 'Permitted Earlier Maturity Debt' p.85; Section 2.16(a), p.132; Section 2.16(d)(i)(B)-(C), p.134
rows.explanation: The headline capacity matches exactly: $331m / 100% of EBITDA fixed amount, 3.50x / 4.00x ratio tests and the $83m / 25% earlier-maturity basket. The CA adds a $25m minimum, a Latest Maturity Date test and no-netting of proceeds, and makes LCT testing (a Company election under the TS) also subject to the incremental lenders' agreement. These are modest lender-favourable tightenings. One point goes the other way: Section 2.16(a)(vi) lets incremental term loan terms 'reflect market terms' instead of being no more restrictive than existing terms, which loosens the TS protection for existing lenders and favours the borrower.

rows.attribute: Benchmark rates, floors and credit spread adjustment
rows.ts_value: Company's option: Term SOFR, Alternative Currency Daily Rate or Alternative Currency Term Rate, each floored at 0%, plus the Applicable Margin; or, for USD, Base Rate (highest of Federal Funds Rate + 1/2%, BofA prime, and Term SOFR + 1.00%) plus the Applicable Margin. No credit spread adjustment. USD swingline accrues at Base Rate plus the Base Rate margin. EUR swingline rate is a 'customary rate ... to be determined'.
rows.ts_quote: Each Swingline Loan denominated in U.S. dollars shall bear interest at the Base Rate plus the Applicable Margin for Base Rate loans under the New Revolving Credit Facility.
rows.ca_value: Term SOFR (0% floor). Alternative Currency Daily Rate (SONIA for Sterling; 0% floor). Alternative Currency Term Rate (EURIBOR, Term CORRA, TIBOR, BBSY; 0% floor). Base Rate is the highest of Federal Funds Rate + 1/2%, BofA prime and Term SOFR + 1.00%. No SOFR or credit spread adjustment. USD swingline accrues at the SOFR Daily Floating Rate (the one-month Term SOFR Screen Rate reset each Business Day; 0% floor) plus the Term SOFR-column Applicable Rate. EUR swingline accrues at Basic ESTR (0% floor) plus the same Applicable Rate.
rows.ca_quote: (v) each Swing Line Loan denominated in Dollars shall bear interest on the outstanding principal amount thereof from the applicable borrowing date at a rate per annum equal to the SOFR Daily Floating Rate plus the Applicable Rate
rows.ca_location: Section 1.01 'Alternative Currency Daily Rate' p.37, 'Alternative Currency Term Rate' p.38, 'Base Rate' pp.42-43, 'Basic ESTR' p.43, 'SOFR Daily Floating Rate' p.92, 'Term SOFR' pp.95-96; Section 2.04(a), p.116; Section 2.08(a), PDF p.124
rows.explanation: The main benchmarks, 0% floors, Base Rate definition and absence of a credit spread adjustment all match, and the open EUR swingline rate is filled in as Basic ESTR. USD swingline pricing differs: the TS says Base Rate + Base Rate margin, the CA uses one-month Term SOFR (reset daily) + the SOFR margin. The Base Rate is at least Term SOFR + 1.00%, and the Base Rate margin is exactly 1.00% below the SOFR margin at every level. So the CA rate is never higher, and it is lower by roughly (prime - Term SOFR - 1.00%), typically about 2%, whenever prime sets the Base Rate. This favours the borrower.

rows.ts_value: While any default continues, the Applicable Margin on all obligations rises by 2% p.a. This is automatic for a principal payment default; in all other cases it applies on request of the Required Lenders.

It applies: (i) automatically to overdue principal only; (ii) to other overdue amounts on Required Lenders' request; (iii) to all outstanding Obligations while an Event of Default exists, on Required Lenders' request. LC fees go to the Default Rate during an Event of Default at the request of the Required Revolving Lenders.

rows.ts_value: Amortization for each term loan: 0.625% quarterly for the first eight payment dates, then 1.25% quarterly, with the balance at maturity. Payments fall on the third business day after each quarter-end, starting after the first full fiscal quarter following the Effective Date. Mandatory prepayment of 100% of asset sale, insurance and condemnation net cash proceeds above $25m per fiscal year, with a $10m per-transaction de minimis. Reinvestment within 365 days, or 545 days if committed within 365. 100% of proceeds of non-permitted debt. Application: to the term facilities the Company chooses, pro rata, next four installments in direct order then pro rata. Lenders may decline asset-sale prepayments. Exception for material adverse tax consequences of repatriation. Payment may be deferred to avoid breakage for up to 30 days, or longer if the Administrative Agent agrees.
rows.ts_quote: subject to reinvestment provisions (which will include the right to reinvest in other assets within 365 days of receipt (or, if the Company or the applicable subsidiary has entered into a binding commitment with respect to such reinvestment within such 365 day period, within 545 days of receipt))
rows.ts_location: PDF pp.12-13, 'Scheduled Amortization/Availability'; pp.13-14, 'Mandatory Prepayments and Commitment Reductions'
rows.ca_value: Section 2.07(a)-(b): 0.625% for the first eight quarterly payment dates, then 1.250%, on the third Business Day after each quarter-end starting after the first full fiscal quarter; the balance is due at the Maturity Date. Section 2.05(b): 100% of Disposition and Extraordinary Receipt (insurance/condemnation) Net Cash Proceeds, excluding transactions under $10,000,000 and the first $25,000,000 per fiscal year. Sub-$10m transactions count toward the $25m annual allowance, which is shared between Dispositions and Extraordinary Receipts. Reinvestment within 365/545 days, but only on an election notified on or before the Disposition date and only 'so long as no Default shall have occurred and be continuing'. 100% of proceeds of debt not permitted under Section 7.02. Application matches the TS (Company-directed, next four installments, then pro rata). Lenders may decline prepayments under (b)(i)/(iii). The tax exception is limited to Foreign Subsidiary proceeds that need an upstream distribution, and it includes a catch-up obligation to prepay once the restriction lapses. Breakage deferral is capped at 30 days, with no Administrative Agent extension.
rows.ca_quote: so long as no Default shall have occurred and be continuing, the Company or such Restricted Subsidiary may reinvest all or any portion of such Net Cash Proceeds in operating assets or assets useful in the business
rows.ca_location: Section 2.07(a)-(b), PDF p.123; Section 2.05(b)(i)-(viii), pp.119-122; Section 1.01 'Extraordinary Receipt', p.68
rows.explanation: The amortization schedule, sweep percentages, $25m/$10m thresholds, 365/545-day reinvestment periods, application waterfall and declined-amount mechanics all match. The CA adds a no-Default condition and an advance-election requirement for reinvestment. It also narrows the tax-repatriation exception to Foreign Subsidiaries and adds a catch-up prepayment once the restriction lapses, counts de minimis transactions toward the $25m annual allowance, and removes the Administrative Agent's ability to extend the 30-day breakage deferral.

The operative terms are in the conformed copy attached as Exhibit A, which starts at PDF p.28. The conformed copy's own page numbers in its table of contents do not match PDF page numbers, and all CA page references here are PDF pages. The reconciliation is against the agreement as amended. rows.attribute: Security / collateral, including any fall-away or springback
rows.ts_value:
Collateral package: each domestic Loan Party grants first-priority liens over (i) all subsidiary equity (65% of CFC stock), (ii) intercompany debt owed to Grantors, and (iii) all personal property and proceeds. The collateral secures the facilities plus designated treasury management and hedging, subject to listed Excluded Assets. Control agreements are required only on a commercially reasonable efforts basis, only on AA request, only for US deposit accounts (none for accounts with average daily balance below $5M) and securities accounts not held with Lenders. Only US-law security documents are required.

Release: on Company request with certification, if either (a) CNLR is below 2.00x for the last two quarters and pro forma, or (b) a Ratings Release Trigger Event occurs (two of Moody's Baa3 / S&P BBB- / Fitch BBB-, each with stable outlook), and in either case there is no default and no Financial Covenant Adjustment.

Springback: a Collateral Reinstatement Event requires both (a) CNLR of 2.50x or more (quarterly) or 3.00x or more (pro forma), and (b) two of three ratings at Ba1/BB+ or below, or unrated.

All collateral is released on payment in full, regardless of outstanding hedging or cash management.

rows.ts_location: PDF pp.14-17, 'Security' and 'Release of Collateral and Reinstatement of collateral' (quote p.17)
rows.ca_value:
Collateral package: under the Collateral and Guarantee Requirement, each Domestic Obligor grants security over substantially all assets other than Excluded Assets and pledges subsidiary equity (CFC and Foreign Holding Company pledges limited to 65% of voting and 100% of non-voting interests). Control agreements are required on a commercially reasonable efforts basis, at AA request, only for Material Deposit Accounts (average daily balance over $10M) and Material Securities Accounts (over $5M) not held with Lenders. There are no non-US security documents, and Excluded Assets are listed in proviso (i)-(xvii), which also exclude letter-of-credit rights not perfectible by UCC filing and commercial tort claims below $25M. Secured obligations also include Bilateral Foreign Loan Facilities.

Release: the Collateral Release Event uses the same 2.00x / ratings / no Default / no FCA tests, plus a new condition (e): no other Indebtedness may remain secured by the Collateral unless permitted under s.7.01 (excluding s.7.01(l)). Release is automatic (s.10.22(a)).

Springback: the Collateral Reinstatement Event uses the same 2.50x/3.00x and ratings tests or, alternatively, (y) the incurrence of other Indebtedness secured by assets that would have been Collateral, unless those Liens are permitted under s.7.01 (excluding s.7.01(l)). Reinstatement must be completed within 30 days (extendable by the AA).

On release at the Facility Termination Date, hedge, cash management and bilateral foreign facility obligations are excluded.
rows.ca_quote: or (y) the incurrence of any other Indebtedness secured by assets and property that would have constituted Collateral under this Agreement if the Collateral were still in place

rows.explanation: The core collateral package, the release tests (2.00x or investment-grade ratings) and the springback tests (2.50x/3.00x plus sub-investment-grade ratings) match. However, the CA adds a no-other-secured-debt condition to release and an alternative springback trigger on incurrence of other secured debt (lender favourable), extends secured obligations to Bilateral Foreign Loan Facilities, and requires 100% of non-voting CFC/FHC equity (TS: 65% of CFC stock). In the other direction, it raises the deposit-account control threshold from $5M to $10M, adds a $5M securities-account threshold, applies the 65% cap to Foreign Holding Companies and excludes letter-of-credit rights and smaller commercial tort claims (borrower favourable).

Basket amounts: ss.7.01, 7.02, 7.03, 7.05, 7.06 and the 'Cumulative Available Amount' definition carry over every TS dollar and percentage amount, including:
- Debt: s.7.02(n) $165M/50%; (i), (l), (o) $115M/35%; (j) $150M; (e) $165M/50%; (q) $115M/35%; (h) $75M early maturity / 5.00x; (c) $250M/75%.
- Liens: s.7.01(i) $165M/50%; (k) $150M.
- Investments: s.7.03(l) $250M/75%; (k) $115M/35%; (f) 3.50x; (c) $250M/75%; (b) $10M; (m) AAB subject to no Specified Default.
- RPs: s.7.06(f) $100M/30%; (g) 3.00x; (d) $33M/10%; (h) $30M/5%; (i) buybacks.
- Dispositions: s.7.05(l) $25M / 75% / $83M / 25%; (h) $50M; (f) $50M.
- CAA starter: $165M/50%.

Differences:
- Permitted Acquisitions require that no Default of any kind exists, and also require a same or related line of business, no materially adverse contingent liabilities, a consensual (board-approved) target and, above $100M, advance notice and an officer's certificate.
- The ratio RP basket requires CNLR 'less than' 3.00x.
- The general RP basket and PPCR RPs require no Default.
- Secured acquired debt is capped at $50M (s.7.01(h)).
- General-basket liens may not attach to Collateral outside a Collateral Release Period.
- Unsecured debt maturing after the latest Maturity Date must also be on terms reasonably acceptable to the AA (s.7.02(h)(ii)(B)).
- The intercompany cap applies to non-Loan Party-to-Loan Party and Foreign-Obligor-to-Domestic-Obligor debt, with subordination of Domestic-to-Foreign and Loan Party-to-non-Loan Party debt above $10M.
- The CAA builders count the fair market value of non-cash equity proceeds and contributions and the principal of debt converted into equity (TS: net cash proceeds), but credit retained asset-sale proceeds only if not reinvested.
- The CA adds baskets: $25M non-debt liens, a $150M Bilateral Foreign Loan Facility cap, convertible notes / bond hedge RPs, and unlimited disposal of non-core acquired assets.
rows.ca_quote: (e) (A) immediately before and immediately after giving pro forma effect to any such Acquisition, no Default shall have occurred and be continuing
rows.ca_location: ss.7.01-7.06 (PDF pp.167-175); 'Permitted Acquisition' (pp.83-85, quote p.84); 'Cumulative Available Amount' (pp.59-60); 'Specified Default' (p.93)
rows.explanation: All TS basket amounts are carried into the CA. However, the CA conditions Permitted Acquisitions on the absence of any Default, not just payment or bankruptcy Events of Default, and adds line-of-business, consensual-target and $100M notice conditions, which materially tightens acquisition flexibility. It also adds several smaller lender-favourable conditions: a strict below-3.00x RP test, no-Default conditions, a $50M cap on secured acquired debt, no general-basket liens on Collateral and AA-acceptable terms for long-dated unsecured debt. The broader CAA builders and the unlimited non-core asset disposals are borrower favourable, but the net effect remains lender favourable.

The restricted group must represent at least 90% of consolidated total assets and at least 90% of Consolidated EBITDA. No restricted subsidiary or Loan Party that owns or holds exclusive licenses to material IP may be designated. No investment, RP or disposition of Material IP to unrestricted subsidiaries is permitted, and no unrestricted subsidiary may own or hold Material IP.

TS: "Summary of Principal Terms and Conditions" for Quaker Chemical Corporation, "$[1.55][1.6] BILLION SENIOR SECURED CREDIT FACILITIES", marked "Posting Version 3/25/26". It runs 27 pages plus Addendum I (pricing, fees and expenses) at PDF pp.28-29. It is a formal pre-syndication term sheet, still showing bracketed facility amounts and pricing, and is framed as an amendment (or amendment and restatement) of the August 1, 2019 Existing Credit Agreement.

CA: Amendment No. 4 to Credit Agreement dated April 10, 2026, filed as Exhibit 10.1 (PDF pp.1-27, including the conditions precedent, reaffirmation and signature pages). Its Exhibit A is a conformed copy of the Credit Agreement dated August 1, 2019, as amended by Amendments No. 1 (Mar 17, 2020), No. 2 (Dec 10, 2021), No. 3 (Jun 17, 2022) and No. 4 (PDF pp.28-213). Reconciliation was performed against the agreement as amended (Exhibit A) together with the Amendment's own conditions and reaffirmations.

Limitations:
- The extracted CA text ends at Section 10.23 (PDF p.213). Exhibit B (schedules, including Schedule 2.01 commitments) and Exhibit C (exhibits, e.g. the Guaranty (Exhibit F), the Security and Pledge Agreement forms and Appendix A Dutch Auction procedures) are not in the text. Guarantee and collateral terms were therefore reconciled only as reflected in the Credit Agreement itself.
- The pre-amendment Existing Credit Agreement was not provided. TS items expressly tied to it (event-of-default grace periods and materiality thresholds, bail-in) were checked only against the amended text.
- PDF page rendering was unavailable (pdftoppm not installed). No Group B item depended on a garbled table.
- Group A economics (amounts, pricing, maturities, accordion/incremental, prepayments) were excluded per instructions. Swingline mechanics (minimum amounts, 10-business-day repayment) were treated as Group A sublimit terms.

CA drafting observations:
- In the extracted text, Section 7.11 labels two clauses "(a)", and its proviso refers to an undefined "Consolidated Senior Net Leverage Ratio".
- Some sub-clause letters in Sections 5.05, 9.01, 10.04 and 10.06 are mis-sequenced in the text, so the cross-reference lettering was used. In s.5.05, the audited and unaudited financial statement reps are both lettered "(a)". As a result, the s.4.02(a) deeming rule for "Sections 5.05(a) and (b)" reaches only the financial-statement reps, and the no-MAE rep (lettered "(b)") is brought down at each Credit Extension.
- The repeating no-MAE representation in Section 5.05 refers to December 31, 2021, although the Audited Financial Statements run to December 31, 2025 and the Amendment No. 4 closing MAE condition uses December 31, 2025.

rows.ca_value: The Commitment Termination Date is the earliest of five dates. (a) The fifth anniversary of the Amendment No. 2 Effective Date (the Scheduled Commitment Termination Date); 'Amendment No. 2' is inserted. (b) Facility Termination. (c) The Notes Early Termination Date, defined as 91 days before the Scheduled Commitment Termination Date, but only if Second Lien Notes are still outstanding on that date. The 5-year tenor matches, as does the rule that unsecured or junior debt must mature at least 91 days after the Scheduled Commitment Termination Date. The springing maturity does not match.

- TS: the facility matures 91 days before the Second Lien Notes' stated maturity whenever that comes before the 5-year date.
- CA: the test date is 91 days before the RCF's own 5-year date, and it only applies if Second Lien Notes are still outstanding then. It can therefore never bring maturity forward to the notes' maturity.

The CA also drops the Liquidity Early Termination Date, which the TS never mentions. The Notes Early Termination Date definition has no redline, and the TS describes the existing facility in the same words, so the TS wording may be shorthand. Confirm with the deal team.

result.document_notes:
TS: not a formal term sheet. It is a 38-page J.P. Morgan "Lender Presentation" dated May 2026 for Seadrill Limited / Seadrill Finance Limited. Deal terms appear only in the "Summary terms and conditions" table on PDF pp.35-36, which has Existing and Proposed columns, plus the timeline on p.37. The layout text of the p.35 grid is misaligned (row labels and values are offset, and the >=/<= signs are lost). Row alignment (pricing tiers, L/C sublimit, accordion, anti cash hoarding) was checked against a raw-order pdftotext extraction of the same PDF pages. The TS says nothing about currencies, interest periods, minimum amounts, default interest, L/C fees, swingline or extension options. The other p.35-36 items (guarantors, collateral release, financial covenants, cash netting, restricted payments, investments, liens/debt baskets, asset sales) are not commercial or economic terms for group A, so they are not reconciled here.

CA: a Form 8-K (signed June 18, 2026) attaching Exhibit 10.1, Amendment No. 2 dated June 16, 2026 to the Senior Secured Revolving Credit Agreement dated July 11, 2023 (as amended by Amendment No. 1 dated April 3, 2026). Its terms take effect on the Amendment No. 2 Effective Date (the 8-K expects June 30, 2026). The amendment attaches, as Exhibit A (cover p.33), a conformed copy of the credit agreement (PDF pp.34-231) shown as a redline. The pdftotext output keeps the struck text and runs it together with the inserted text (e.g. "onas of", "(cb)", "LondonNew York City"), and the old 0.10% CSA and 0.50%/0.75%/1.00% step-up definitions still appear.

How the redline was read: the PDF cannot be rendered here (no pdftoppm), so the ASCII85/Flate page content streams were decoded read-only. Changed text is set in a bold (or bold-italic) font. Struck text has a line drawn about 2pt above the baseline; inserted text has a line drawn below the baseline. On review, these readings were independently re-verified for: Commitment Termination Date (p.64), Liquidity Early Termination Date (p.86, struck in full), Notes Early Termination Date (p.88, unchanged), Revolving Credit Commitment Amount (p.100), Floor (p.78), Adjusted Term SOFR Rate (p.45, struck in full), Applicable Margin (p.50: grid unchanged, 3rd-Business-Day lag inserted, Level II retained), Commitment Fee Rate (p.63, only 'a rate per annum equal to 0.50%' survives), Business Day (p.60, 'and London' struck), and s.2.6/s.2.7 ('Adjusted' struck). Some quotes therefore contain text that is struck in the PDF, and the explanation says so where it matters.

Limitations:
- Annexes II-VII are omitted under Item 601(a)(5), including Schedule 2.12(a), which sets each Issuing Bank's Maximum L/C Issuance Amount.
- Schedule 1 / Annex I (the commitment schedule, pp.32 and 232) is included but its text is garbled. The four $62.5mm entries and one $50mm entry total $300mm.
- No fee letter for the 2026 transaction is included.
- The Second Lien Notes' stated maturity does not appear in either document.

result.document_notes:
TS: this is not a formal term sheet. It is a 38-page J.P. Morgan-led "Lender Presentation" dated May 2026 for Seadrill Limited. Pages 1-33 are marketing and financial material (fleet, backlog, projections, capital allocation policy) and contain no facility terms. The terms are in the "Summary terms and conditions" table on PDF pp.35-36, which has Existing and Proposed columns, and the indicative timeline on p.37.

In the pdftotext -layout extraction the table is partly garbled. Labels and values sit on different lines, and the value block runs below its labels. The <=/>= symbols are dropped (for example "Net Leverage  3.00x"), but literal "<" and ">" survive. Row mapping was confirmed by counting value blocks in each column:
- p.35: Fin. covenants, then L/C sublimit $100mm, Accordion $100mm, Anti-cash hoarding $250mm, then Cash netting.
- p.36: RP (4 bullets), Permitted investments $100mm, LCE, Secured (4 items), Specified bilateral ($25mm to $100mm), 2L/Junior, Unsecured/General, Asset sales, Fees.

Some -layout lines splice Existing and Proposed column text. Quotes taken from such lines can be verbatim but misleading (corrected in B02).

Upfront fee, facility size, maturity, pricing grid, CSA, commitment fee, L/C sublimit and accordion are Group A and are not reconciled here. For the Group A analyst: the TS says the facility is "Up to $275mm" but the CA commitments are $300m (Annex I).

CA: a Seadrill Limited Form 8-K (event date June 16, 2026; signed June 18, 2026). It attaches Exhibit 10.1, Amendment No. 2 dated June 16, 2026, to the Senior Secured Revolving Credit Agreement dated July 11, 2023, which was previously amended by Amendment No. 1 dated April 3, 2026. The Amendment is effective on the Amendment No. 2 Effective Date; the 8-K says this is expected on June 30, 2026. The filing includes Exhibit A, a conformed blackline of the Credit Agreement (PDF pp.34-231), with Annex I (Schedule 1.1(c) commitments) at p.232. The reconciliation is against the agreement as amended.

In the blackline text, deleted and inserted text run together, with the deleted text first (e.g. "$225,000,000300,000,000", "1.001.75", "8075%"). This order is confirmed by:
- the 8-K's description of a $225m to $300m upsize
- the Exhibit A cover legend "Conformed to reflect changes effected by Amendment No. 12, dated April 3June 16, 2026"

Strikethrough cannot be seen in the text, and PDF page rendering and PDF libraries were not available. Wholly struck passages therefore cannot be told apart from live text. In particular, Harsh Environment references still appear in the Collateral Rig and Guarantor definitions, §4.2(vii), §6.17 and the §7.9(b) proviso. They no longer operate in any case, because Amendment §1(d) deletes Schedule 1.1(r), the schedule of Harsh Environment Rigs and Subsidiaries. §10.8(c)(ii) and §11.30(b)(y) expressly read "[reserved]".

Limitations: schedules and annexes were omitted under Reg. S-K Item 601(a)(5). These include:
- Annex II (new Schedule 1.1(e), whose Part A lists the Non-Core Rigs)
- Annex VI (Part A Released Guarantors, Part B Released Rigs, Part C release documents)
- Schedule 5.20 (Amendment No. 2 Effective Date Guarantors)
- Schedule 5.21 (Collateral Rigs)
- Schedule 2.12(a) (Issuing Banks)
- Amendment Schedule 2 (deliverables)

As a result, the names of the released rigs and guarantors (e.g. West Phoenix, West Aquarius, West Eclipse) cannot be verified. Fee letters were not filed, so the JLA fee cannot be checked against the CA. The CA's table of contents is garbled by the blackline; section numbers and page references are taken from the body text and the [PDF PAGE n] markers.

Review result: every quote in the first pass was checked mechanically and found verbatim. All numeric terms were re-verified against the CA body:
- §7.2, §7.3, §7.5, §7.7 and §7.11
- the Permitted Investment, Specified Bilateral Obligations, Second Lien Notes, Agreed Security Principles (r), Consolidated Total Indebtedness and Permitted Additional Debt definitions
- §4.3 and §8.1

The corrections are limited to:
- one misleading spliced TS quote (B02)
- two page references (B07, B16)
- a cross-default characterisation (B12)
- a consent-party omission (B15)
- explanatory caveats on the Harsh Environment deletion (B02, B06) and on the Specified Bilateral Obligations inconsistency (X11)

No TS term outside Group A was missing from the row list.
